<h1 id="mollie-api-payouts-api">Payouts API</h1>

Operations related to the Payouts API

## List payouts

<a id="opIdlist-payouts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/payouts \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/payouts`

Retrieve a list of all payouts for your organization, including payouts initiated automatically by the
balance's payout schedule and payouts requested via the API or dashboard.

Only payouts created on or after April 1st, 2026 are returned.

The results are paginated. Use the `from` query parameter together with `_links.next` to iterate through
the full result set.

<h3 id="list-payouts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|balanceId|query|string \| null|false|Return only payouts for the balance with the given ID. The value must be a valid balance<br>token in the format `bal_*`.|
|from|query|string \| null|false|Provide an ID to start the result set from the item with the given ID and onwards. This allows you to paginate the<br>result set.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50 items.|
|sort|query|[sorting](#schemasorting)|false|Used for setting the direction of the result set. Defaults to descending order, meaning the results are ordered from<br>newest to oldest.|
|testmode|query|boolean|false|Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode. In those cases the `testmode` query<br>parameter must not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by<br>setting the `testmode` query parameter to `true`.<br><br>Test entities cannot be retrieved when the endpoint is set to live mode, and vice versa.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Create payout

<a id="opIdcreate-payout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/payouts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "balanceId": "bal_gVMhHKqSSRYJyPsuoPNFH",
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "description": "My payout description",
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/payouts`

Request a payout from one of your balances to the balance's configured bank account.

The payout will be executed on the next scheduled business day. If no `amount` is specified, the full available
balance minus any configured balance reserve is paid out.

Once the payout is created with status `requested`, you can cancel it via the
[Cancel payout](cancel-payout) endpoint, up until the payout moves to `initiated`.

Creating a payout via the API automatically sets the balance's `transferFrequency` to `never`,
pausing any previously configured automatic settlement schedule. To resume automatic settlements,
update the transfer frequency via the dashboard.

### Webhooks

Subscribe to the following webhook events to track payout status changes. See the
[Webhook Subscriptions API](list-webhooks) for details on subscribing.

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `payout.initiated` | The payout is being executed and funds are reserved. |
| `payout.processing-at-bank` | The payout has been submitted to the bank. |
| `payout.completed` | The payout has been sent to the destination bank account. |
| `payout.canceled` | The payout was canceled via the API before being submitted to the bank. |
| `payout.failed` | The payout failed after creation, including bank rejections and post-submission cancellations. |

### Payout failure reasons

A payout request may fail immediately if one of the following conditions applies:

- A payout is already scheduled for the next business day for this balance.
- The balance has insufficient funds.
- The balance is not active.
- Payouts are blocked for this organization.
- The balance has queued refunds.
- One of the organization's balances is below the negative balance threshold.
- The payout destination (bank account) is invalid or not configured.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "balanceId": "bal_gVMhHKqSSRYJyPsuoPNFH",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "description": "My payout description",
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-payout-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[payout-request](#schemapayout-request)|true|none|
|» balanceId|body|string|true|The identifier of the balance that will be paid out. Example: `bal_gVMhHKqSSRYJyPsuoPNFH`.|
|» amount|body|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|false|The amount to pay out. When omitted from the request, the full available balance minus any configured<br>balance reserve is paid out.<br><br>Merchants registered in the United Kingdom cannot specify a custom amount — omit this field to pay out<br>the full available balance.<br><br>The value in the response reflects the amount paid out, excluding any applicable fees.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|The description that will appear on the bank statement for this payout.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json

  "resource": "payout",
  "id": "payout_j8NvRAM2WNZtsykpLEX8J",
  "balanceId": "bal_gVMhHKqSSRYJyPsuoPNFH",

    "currency": "EUR",

  },

  },

    "self": {
      "href": "https://api.mollie.com/v2/payouts/payout_j8NvRAM2WNZtsykpLEX8J",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "documentation": {

      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

## Cancel payout

<a id="opIdcancel-payout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/payouts/payout_j8NvRAM2WNZtsykpLEX8J \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/payouts/{payoutId}`

Cancel a payout. A payout can only be canceled while it has the status `requested`. Once the payout moves
to `initiated`, it is too late to cancel.

The canceled payout object is returned with the status set to `canceled`.

For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by<br>setting the `testmode` query parameter to `true`.<br><br>Test entities cannot be retrieved when the endpoint is set to live mode, and vice versa.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|payoutId|path|string|true|Provide the ID of the payout.|

|count|[list-count](#schemalist-count)|true|none|The number of items in this result set. If more items are available, a `_links.next` URL will be present in the result<br>as well.<br><br>The maximum number of items per result set is controlled by the `limit` property provided in the request. The default<br>limit is 50 items.|
|_embedded|object|true|none|none|
|» permissions|[[list-entity-permission](#schemalist-entity-permission)]|true|none|An array of permission objects.|
|_links|object|true|none|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|
|» self|[url](#schemaurl)|true|none|The URL to the current set of items.|
|» documentation|[url](#schemaurl)|true|none|In v2 endpoints, URLs are commonly represented as objects with an `href` and `type` field.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## List profiles

<a id="opIdlist-profiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/profiles \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/profiles`

Retrieve a list of all of your profiles.

The results are paginated.

<h3 id="list-profiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string \| null|false|Provide an ID to start the result set from the item with the given ID and onwards. This allows you to paginate the<br>result set.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50 items.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "_embedded": {
    "profiles": [
      {
        "resource": "profile",
        "id": "pfl_QkEhN94Ba",
        "mode": "live",
        "name": "My website name",
        "website": "https://shop.example.org",
        "email": "info@example.org",
        "phone": "+31208202070",
        "businessCategory": "OTHER_MERCHANDISE",
        "status": "verified",
        "review": {
          "status": "pending"
        },
        "createdAt": "2023-03-20T09:28:37+00:00",
        "_links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "...",
            "type": "application/hal+json"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "previous": null,
    "next": {
      "href": "https://api.mollie.com/v2/profiles?from=pfl_v9hTwCvYqw&limit=5",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "detail": "Invalid cursor value",
  "field": "from",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "detail": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please slow down your requests.",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://docs.mollie.com/overview/handling-errors",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-profiles-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A list of profile objects.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request contains issues. For example, if the specified `from` value is not a valid ID.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit has been reached.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<h3 id="list-profiles-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|[list-count](#schemalist-count)|true|none|The number of items in this result set. If more items are available, a `_links.next` URL will be present in the result<br>as well.<br><br>The maximum number of items per result set is controlled by the `limit` property provided in the request. The default<br>limit is 50 items.|
|_embedded|object|true|none|none|
|» profiles|[[list-profile-response](#schemalist-profile-response)]|true|none|An array of profile objects.|
|_links|[list-links](#schemalist-links)|true|none|Links to help navigate through the lists of items. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Create profile

<a id="opIdcreate-profile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/profiles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My website name",
    "website": "https://example.com",
    "email": "test@mollie.com",
    "phone": "+31208202070",
    "description": "My website description",
    "countriesOfActivity": [
      "NL",
      "GB"
    ],
    "businessCategory": "OTHER_MERCHANDISE"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/profiles`

Create a profile to process payments on.

Profiles are required for payment processing. Normally they are created via the Mollie dashboard. Alternatively, you
can use this endpoint to automate profile creation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My website name",
  "website": "https://example.com",
  "email": "test@mollie.com",
  "phone": "+31208202070",
  "description": "My website description",
  "countriesOfActivity": [
    "NL",
    "GB"
  ],
  "businessCategory": "OTHER_MERCHANDISE"
}
```

<h3 id="create-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[profile-request](#schemaprofile-request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The profile's name, this will usually reflect the trade name or brand name of the profile's website or<br>application.|
|» website|body|string|true|The URL to the profile's website or application. Only `https` or `http` URLs are allowed. No `@` signs are<br>allowed.|
|» email|body|string|true|The email address associated with the profile's trade name or brand.<br><br>If the domain contains non-ASCII characters, encode it as Punycode per [RFC 3492](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3492).|
|» phone|body|string|true|The phone number associated with the profile's trade name or brand.|
|» description|body|string|false|The products or services offered by the profile's website or application.|
|» countriesOfActivity|body|[string]|false|A list of countries where you expect that the majority of the profile's customers reside,<br>in [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) format.|
|» businessCategory|body|string \| null|false|The industry associated with the profile's trade name or brand. Please refer to the<br>[business category list](common-data-types#business-category) for all possible options.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "resource": "profile",
  "id": "pfl_QkEhN94Ba",
  "mode": "live",
  "name": "My website name",
  "website": "https://shop.example.org",
  "email": "info@example.org",
  "phone": "+31208202070",
  "businessCategory": "OTHER_MERCHANDISE",
  "status": "verified",
  "review": {
    "status": "pending"
  },
  "createdAt": "2023-03-20T09:28:37+00:00",
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "dashboard": {
      "href": "https://www.mollie.com/dashboard/org_123456789/settings/profiles/pfl_QkEhN94Ba",
      "type": "text/html"
    },
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "status": 403,
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "detail": "Profile limit has been reached for demo accounts.",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "status": 422,
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "detail": "The 'website' field is missing",
  "field": "website",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "detail": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please slow down your requests.",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://docs.mollie.com/overview/handling-errors",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created profile object.|[profile-response](#schemaprofile-response)|
|403|Forbidden|Profile limit has been reached for demo accounts.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request contains issues. For example, if a profile name is missing or website URL is invalid.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit has been reached.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
advancedAccessToken, oAuth ( Scopes: profiles.write )
</aside>

## Get current profile

<a id="opIdget-current-profile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/profiles/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/profiles/me`

Retrieve the currently authenticated profile. A convenient alias of the [Get profile](get-profile)
endpoint.

For a complete reference of the profile object, refer to the [Get profile](get-profile) endpoint
documentation.

<h3 id="get-current-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Create payment refund

<a id="opIdcreate-refund"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/payments/tr_5B8cwPMGnU/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Refunding a Chess Board",
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "metadata": "string",
    "reverseRouting": false,
    "routingReversals": [
      {
        "amount": {
          "currency": "EUR",
          "value": "10.00"
        },
        "source": {
          "type": {},
          "organizationId": "org_1234567"
        }
      }
    ],
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/payments/{paymentId}/refunds`

Creates a refund for a specific payment. The refunded amount is credited to your customer usually either via a bank
transfer or by refunding the amount to your customer's credit card.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Refunding a Chess Board",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "metadata": "string",
  "reverseRouting": false,
  "routingReversals": [
    {
      "amount": {
        "currency": "EUR",
        "value": "10.00"
      },
      "source": {
        "type": {},
        "organizationId": "org_1234567"
      }
    }
  ],
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-payment-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|paymentId|path|[paymentToken](#schemapaymenttoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related payment.|
|body|body|[refund-request](#schemarefund-request)|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|The description of the refund that may be shown to your customer, depending on the payment method used.|
|» amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|The amount refunded to your customer with this refund. The amount is allowed to be lower than the original payment<br>amount.|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Provide any data you like, for example a string or a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity. Whenever<br>you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately 1kB.|
|» reverseRouting|body|boolean \| null|false|*This feature is only available to marketplace operators.*<br><br>With Mollie Connect you can charge fees on payments that your app is processing on behalf of other Mollie<br>merchants, by providing the `routing` object during [payment creation](create-payment).<br><br>When creating refunds for these *routed* payments, by default the full amount is deducted from your balance.<br><br>If you want to pull back the funds that were routed to the connected merchant(s), you can set this parameter to<br>`true` when issuing a full refund.<br><br>For more fine-grained control and for partial refunds, use the `routingReversals` parameter instead.|
|» routingReversals|body|[object]|false|*This feature is only available to marketplace operators.*<br><br>When creating refunds for *routed* payments, by default the full amount is deducted from your balance.<br><br>If you want to pull back funds from the connected merchant(s), you can use this parameter to specify what amount<br>needs to be reversed from which merchant(s).<br><br>If you simply want to fully reverse the routed funds, you can also use the `reverseRouting` parameter instead.|
|» » amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|The amount that will be pulled back.|
|» » source|body|object|false|Where the funds will be pulled back from.|
|» » » type|body|object|false|none|
|» » » organizationId|body|[organizationToken](#schemaorganizationtoken)|false|Required for source type `organization`. The ID of the connected organization the funds should be pulled<br>back from.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
  "resource": "refund",
  "id": "re_4qqhO89gsT",
  "mode": "live",
  "description": "Order",
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "5.95"
  },
  "status": "pending",
  "metadata": "{\"bookkeeping_id\":12345}",
```

## Cancel payment refund

<a id="opIdcancel-refund"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/payments/tr_5B8cwPMGnU/refunds/re_5B8cwPMGnU \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/payments/{paymentId}/refunds/{refundId}`

Refunds will be executed with a delay of two hours. Until that time, refunds may be canceled manually via the
Mollie Dashboard, or by using this endpoint.

A refund can only be canceled while its `status` field is either `queued` or `pending`. See the
[Get refund endpoint](get-refund) for more information.

<h3 id="cancel-payment-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by<br>setting the `testmode` query parameter to `true`.<br><br>Test entities cannot be retrieved when the endpoint is set to live mode, and vice versa.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|paymentId|path|[paymentToken](#schemapaymenttoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related payment.|
|refundId|path|[refundToken](#schemarefundtoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related refund.|

<h1 id="mollie-api-reports-api">Reports API</h1>

Operations related to the Reports API

## Create report

<a id="opIdcreate-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reportType": "transaction_margin",
    "fromDate": "2026-08-01",
    "untilDate": "2026-08-31"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reports`

> 🚧 Beta feature
>
> This feature is currently in private beta, and the final specification may still change. To
> join the beta program, reach out to [partners@mollie.com](mailto:partners@mollie.com).

Create a report. Mollie generates it in the background, so you get a `pending` status back right away.

Poll [Get report](get-report) to check on progress, and grab a download link once it's ready.

This needs an organization access token. A token scoped to a single website profile can't be used,
since report data spans the whole organization.

Test mode credentials are rejected, since report data has no live/test distinction.

Creating a report with the exact same parameters while one is already pending or completed doesn't create
a new one. You get the existing report back instead, whatever status it currently has.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reportType": "transaction_margin",
  "fromDate": "2026-08-01",
  "untilDate": "2026-08-31"
}
```

<h3 id="create-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[create-report-request](#schemacreate-report-request)|true|none|
|» reportType|body|[report-type](#schemareport-type)|true|The type of report to generate. Determines which other fields the request needs, and which fields show up<br>on the resulting report.|
|» fromDate|body|string(date)|true|The start date of the report period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Must be strictly before `untilDate`; a<br>report can't cover a single day. Data is available from 2026-01-01 onwards.|
|» untilDate|body|string(date)|true|The end date of the report period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Must be strictly after `fromDate`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reportType|transaction_margin|

Read `status` from the body rather than<br>assuming `202` always means `pending`.|None|

## Get report

<a id="opIdget-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/reports/rpt_XRAG3v9EUyCDcX99pJ2Vc \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reports/{reportId}`

> 🚧 Beta feature
>
> This feature is currently in private beta, and the final specification may still change. To
> join the beta program, reach out to [partners@mollie.com](mailto:partners@mollie.com).

Retrieve a single report by its ID. Poll this to check on a report you created, and to grab a download
link once it's ready.

The download link is pre-signed and freshly generated on every call, and expires 15 minutes after you get
it. If it expires before you download the file, just call this endpoint again for a new one. Expiry of
the link doesn't affect the report itself.

A report that belongs to another organization gets a `404`, same as one that doesn't exist. The same goes
for a credential scoped to a single website profile, or a test mode credential. Reports are
organization-wide with no live/test distinction, so neither can ever own a real report. That keeps the
rule simple: any credential that can't own this report gets a `404`, and we never leak whether it exists.

<h3 id="get-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|reportId|path|[reportToken](#schemareporttoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related report.|

```json
    }

}
```

`POST /v2/sales-invoices`

With the Sales Invoice API you can generate sales invoices to send to your customers.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "testmode": false,
```

<h3 id="create-sales-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[sales-invoice-request](#schemasales-invoice-request)|false|none|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|
|» profileId|body|string \| null|false|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) this entity belongs to.<br><br>Most API credentials are linked to a single profile. In these cases the `profileId` must not be sent in the creation<br>request. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens however, the `profileId` parameter is<br>required.|
|» status|body|string|true|none|
|» vatScheme|body|[sales-invoice-vat-scheme](#schemasales-invoice-vat-scheme)|false|The VAT scheme to create the invoice for. You must be enrolled with One Stop Shop enabled to use it.|
|» vatMode|body|[sales-invoice-vat-mode](#schemasales-invoice-vat-mode)|false|The VAT mode to use for VAT calculation. `exclusive` mode means we will apply the relevant VAT on top of the<br>price. `inclusive` means the prices you are providing to us already contain the VAT you want to apply.|
|» memo|body|string \| null|false|A free-form memo you can set on the invoice, and will be shown on the invoice PDF.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Provide any data you like as a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity. Whenever<br>you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately 1kB.|
|» paymentTerm|body|[sales-invoice-payment-term](#schemasales-invoice-payment-term)|false|The payment term to be set on the invoice.|
|» paymentDetails|body|object|false|Used when setting an invoice to status of `paid`, and will store a payment that fully pays the invoice with the<br>provided details. Required for `paid` status.|
|» emailDetails|body|[sales-invoice-email-details](#schemasales-invoice-email-details)|false|Used when setting an invoice to status of either `issued` or `paid`. Will be used to issue the invoice to the<br>recipient with the provided `subject` and `body`. Required for `issued` status.|
|» customerId|body|string|false|The identifier referring to the [customer](get-customer) you want to attempt an automated payment for. If<br>provided, `mandateId` becomes required as well. Only allowed for invoices with status `paid`.|
|» mandateId|body|string|false|The identifier referring to the [mandate](get-mandate) you want to use for the automated payment. If provided,<br>`customerId` becomes required as well. Only allowed for invoices with status `paid`.|
|» recipientIdentifier|body|string|true|An identifier tied to the recipient data. This should be a unique value based on data your system contains,<br>so that both you and us know who we're referring to. It is a value you provide to us so that recipient management<br>is not required to send a first invoice to a recipient.|
|» recipient|body|[sales-invoice-recipient](#schemasales-invoice-recipient)|true|none|
|» lines|body|[[sales-invoice-line-item](#schemasales-invoice-line-item)]|true|Provide the line items for the invoice. Each line contains details such as a description of the item<br>ordered and its price.<br><br>All lines must have the same currency as the invoice.|
|» discount|body|[sales-invoice-discount](#schemasales-invoice-discount)|false|The discount to be applied to the entire invoice, applied on top of any line item discounts.|
|» isEInvoice|body|boolean|false|This indicates whether the invoice is an e-invoice. The default value is `false` and can't be changed<br>after the invoice has been issued. When `emailDetails` is provided, an additional email is sent to the<br>recipient.<br><br>E-invoicing is only available for merchants based in Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands, and only when<br>the recipient is also located in one of these countries.<br><br>When set to true, the invoice will be delivered via the Peppol network. In this case, the organizationNumber<br>or vatNumber provided must match the identifier the recipient is actually registered with on Peppol,<br>otherwise delivery will fail. Note: for recipients in Germany, the vatNumber is the required identifier<br>for Peppol registration.|
|» status|body|[sales-invoice-status](#schemasales-invoice-status)|true|The status for the invoice to end up in.<br><br>A `draft` invoice is not paid or not sent and can be updated after creation. Setting it to `issued` sends it to<br>the recipient so they may then pay through our payment system. To skip our payment process, set this to `paid` to<br>mark it as paid. It can then subsequently be sent as well, same as with `issued`.<br><br>Dependent parameters:<br>  - `paymentDetails` is required if invoice should be set directly to `paid`<br>  - `customerId` and `mandateId` are required if a recurring payment should be used to set the invoice to `paid`<br>  - `emailDetails` optional for `issued` and `paid` to send the invoice by email|
|» paymentDetails|body|[sales-invoice-payment-details](#schemasales-invoice-payment-details)|false|Used when setting an invoice to status of `paid`, and will store a payment that fully pays the invoice with the<br>provided details. Required for `paid` status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» vatScheme|standard|
|» vatScheme|one-stop-shop|
|» vatMode|exclusive|
|» vatMode|inclusive|
|» paymentTerm|7 days|
|» paymentTerm|14 days|
|» paymentTerm|30 days|
|» paymentTerm|45 days|
|» paymentTerm|60 days|
|» paymentTerm|90 days|
|» paymentTerm|120 days|
|» status|draft|
|» status|issued|
|» status|paid|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "resource": "sales-invoice",
  "id": "invoice_4Y0eZitmBnQ6IDoMqZQKh",
  "mode": "live",
  "profileId": "pfl_QkEhN94Ba",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "status": "draft",
  "vatScheme": "standard",
```

<a id="opIdupdate-sales-invoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
      "source": "payment-link",
      "sourceReference": "pl_d9fQur83kFdhH8hIhaZfq"
    },

      "subject": "Your invoice is available",

    },
```

`PATCH /v2/sales-invoices/{salesInvoiceId}`

Certain details of an existing sales invoice can be updated. For `draft` it is all values listed below, but for
statuses `paid` and `issued` there are certain additional requirements (`paymentDetails` and `emailDetails`,
respectively).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "testmode": false,
  "status": "draft",
  "memo": "An updated memo!",
  "paymentTerm": "30 days",
  "paymentDetails": {
    "source": "payment-link",
    "sourceReference": "pl_d9fQur83kFdhH8hIhaZfq"
  },
  "emailDetails": {
    "subject": "Your invoice is available",
    "body": "Please find your invoice enclosed."
  },
  "recipientIdentifier": "customer-xyz-0123",
  "recipient": {
    "type": "consumer",
    "title": "Mrs.",
    "givenName": "Jane",
    "familyName": "Doe",
    "organizationName": "Organization Corp.",
    "organizationNumber": "12345678",
    "vatNumber": "NL123456789B01",
    "email": "example@email.com",
    "phone": "+0123456789",
    "streetAndNumber": "Keizersgracht 126",
    "streetAdditional": "4th floor",
    "postalCode": "5678AB",
    "city": "Amsterdam",
    "region": "Noord-Holland",
    "country": "NL",
    "locale": {}
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "description": "LEGO 4440 Forest Police Station",
      "quantity": 1,
      "vatRate": "21.00",
      "unitPrice": {
        "currency": "EUR",
        "value": "10.00"
      },
      "discount": {
        "type": "amount",
        "value": "10.00"
      }
    }
  ],
  "discount": {
    "type": "amount",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "isEInvoice": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-sales-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|salesInvoiceId|path|[salesInvoiceToken](#schemasalesinvoicetoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related sales invoice.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» testmode|body|[testmode](#schematestmode)|false|Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.<br><br>Test entities cannot be retrieved when the endpoint is set to live mode, and vice versa.|
|» status|body|[sales-invoice-status-update](#schemasales-invoice-status-update)|false|The status for the invoice to end up in.<br><br>Dependent parameters: `paymentDetails` for `paid`, `emailDetails` for `issued` and `paid`.<br><br>To cancel a `paid` invoice, first set the status to `payment-reversed`, then set it to `cancelled`.|
|» memo|body|string \| null|false|A free-form memo you can set on the invoice, and will be shown on the invoice PDF.|
|» paymentTerm|body|[sales-invoice-payment-term](#schemasales-invoice-payment-term)|false|The payment term to be set on the invoice.|
|» paymentDetails|body|[sales-invoice-payment-details](#schemasales-invoice-payment-details)|false|Used when setting an invoice to status of `paid`, and will store a payment that fully pays the invoice with the<br>provided details. Required for `paid` status.|
|» emailDetails|body|[sales-invoice-email-details](#schemasales-invoice-email-details)|false|Used when setting an invoice to status of either `issued` or `paid`. Will be used to issue the invoice to the<br>recipient with the provided `subject` and `body`. Required for `issued` status.|
|» recipientIdentifier|body|string|false|An identifier tied to the recipient data. This should be a unique value based on data your system contains,<br>so that both you and us know who we're referring to. It is a value you provide to us so that recipient management<br>is not required to send a first invoice to a recipient.|
|» recipient|body|[sales-invoice-recipient](#schemasales-invoice-recipient)|false|The recipient object should contain all the information relevant to create an invoice for an intended<br>recipient. This data will be stored, updated, and re-used as appropriate, based on the `recipientIdentifier`.|
|» lines|body|[[sales-invoice-line-item](#schemasales-invoice-line-item)]|false|Provide the line items for the invoice. Each line contains details such as a description of the item<br>ordered and its price.<br><br>All lines must have the same currency as the invoice.|
|» discount|body|[sales-invoice-discount](#schemasales-invoice-discount)|false|The discount to be applied to the entire invoice, possibly on top of the line item discounts.|
|» isEInvoice|body|boolean|false|This indicates whether the invoice is an e-invoice. The default value is `false` and can't be changed<br>after the invoice has been issued. When `emailDetails` is provided, an additional email is sent to the<br>recipient.<br><br>E-invoicing is only available for merchants based in Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands, and only when<br>the recipient is also located in one of these countries.<br><br>When set to true, the invoice will be delivered via the Peppol network. In this case, the `organizationNumber`<br>or `vatNumber` provided must match the identifier the recipient is actually registered with on Peppol,<br>otherwise delivery will fail. Note: for recipients in Germany, the `vatNumber` is the required identifier<br>for Peppol registration.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-patch](#schematestmode-patch)|false|Whether the entity was created in test mode or live mode. This field does not update the mode of the entity.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|draft|
|» status|issued|
|» status|paid|
|» status|cancelled|
|» status|payment-reversed|
|» paymentTerm|7 days|
|» paymentTerm|14 days|
|» paymentTerm|30 days|
|» paymentTerm|45 days|
|» paymentTerm|60 days|
|» paymentTerm|90 days|
|» paymentTerm|120 days|

<h1 id="mollie-api-settlements-api">Settlements API</h1>

Operations related to the Settlements API

## List settlements

<a id="opIdlist-settlements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/settlements \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/settlements`

Retrieve a list of all your settlements.

The results are paginated.

<h3 id="list-settlements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string \| null|false|Provide an ID to start the result set from the item with the given ID and onwards. This allows you to paginate the<br>result set.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50 items.|
|balanceId|query|[balanceToken](#schemabalancetoken)|false|Provide the token of the balance to filter the settlements by. This is<br>the balance token that the settlement was settled to.|
|year|query|string \| null|false|Provide the year to query the settlements. Must be used combined with `month` parameter|
|month|query|string \| null|false|Provide the month to query the settlements. Must be used combined with `year` parameter|
|currencies|query|[currencies](#schemacurrencies)|false|Provides the currencies to retrieve the settlements. It accepts multiple currencies in a comma-separated format.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|currencies|EUR|
|currencies|GBP|
|currencies|CHF|
|currencies|DKK|
|currencies|NOK|
|currencies|PLN|
|currencies|SEK|
|currencies|USD|
|currencies|CZK|
|currencies|HUF|
|currencies|AUD|
|currencies|CAD|
|currencies|RON|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 1,
  "_embedded": {
    "settlements": [
      {
        "resource": "settlement",
        "id": "stl_jDk30akdN",
        "reference": "1234567.2404.03",
        "status": "paidout",
        "createdAt": "2024-04-31T12:50:14+00:00",
        "amount": {
          "currency": "EUR",
          "value": "39.75"
        },
        "balanceId": "bal_3kUf4yU2nT",
        "periods": {},
        "settledAt": "2024-04-06T09:41:44+00:00",
        "invoiceId": "inv_FrvewDA3Pr",
        "_links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "...",
            "type": "application/hal+json"
```

## Get settlement

<a id="opIdget-settlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/settlements/stl_5B8cwPMGnU \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/settlements/{settlementId}`

Retrieve a single settlement by its ID.

To lookup settlements by their bank reference, replace the ID in the URL by
a reference. For example: `1234567.2404.03`.

A settlement represents a transfer of your balance funds to your external bank account.

Settlements will typically include a report that details what balance transactions have taken place between this
settlement and the previous one.

For more accurate bookkeeping, refer to the [balance report](get-balance-report) endpoint or the
[balance transactions](list-balance-transactions) endpoint.

<h3 id="get-settlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|settlementId|path|[settlementToken](#schemasettlementtoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related settlement.|

## Get open settlement

<a id="opIdget-open-settlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/settlements/open \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/settlements/open`

Retrieve the details of the open balance of the organization. This will return a settlement object representing your
organization's balance.

For a complete reference of the settlement object, refer to the [Get settlement endpoint](get-settlement)
documentation.

For more accurate bookkeeping, refer to the [balance report](get-balance-report) endpoint or the
[balance transactions](list-balance-transactions) endpoint.

<h3 id="get-open-settlement-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a settlement object. Will always contain the string `settlement` for this<br>endpoint.|
|id|string|true|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this settlement.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|reference|string \| null|false|read-only|The settlement's bank reference, as found in your Mollie account and on your bank statement.|
|settledAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date on which the settlement was settled, in ISO 8601 format.<br><br>For an [open settlement](get-open-settlement) or for the [next settlement](get-next-settlement), no settlement<br>date is available.|
|status|object|true|read-only|none|
|amount|object|true|read-only|none|
|» currency|string|true|none|A three-character ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» value|string|true|none|A string containing an exact monetary amount in the given currency.|
|balanceId|object|true|read-only|The balance token that the settlement was settled to.|
|invoiceId|string \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the oldest invoice created for all the periods, if the invoice has been created yet.|
|periods|object|false|read-only|For bookkeeping purposes, the settlement includes an overview of transactions included in the settlement. These<br>transactions are grouped into 'period' objects — one for each calendar month.<br><br>For example, if a settlement includes funds from 15 April until 4 May, it will include two period objects. One for<br>all transactions processed between 15 April and 30 April, and one for all transactions between 1 May and 4 May.<br><br>Period objects are grouped by year, and then by month. So in the above example, the full `periods` collection will<br>look as follows: `{"2024": {"04": {...}, "05": {...}}}`. The year and month in this documentation are referred as `<year>` and `<month>`.<br><br>The example response should give a good idea of what this looks like in practise.|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » costs|[object]|false|none|An array of cost objects, describing the fees withheld for each payment method during this period.|
|» » » » description|string|true|none|A description of the cost subtotal|
|» » » » method|[settlement-method](#schemasettlement-method)|true|none|The method the cost or revenue subtotal applies to. This is usually a payment method, but can also represent a<br>correction or transaction type that is not tied to a specific payment method.|
|» » » » count|integer|true|none|The number of fees|
|» » » » rate|object|true|none|The service rates, further divided into `fixed` and `percentage` costs.<br><br>For pass-through fees, which are charged by an external party rather than at an agreed Mollie<br>rate, both `fixed` and `percentage` are `null`.|
|» » » » » fixed|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|In v2 endpoints, monetary amounts are represented as objects with a `currency` and `value` field.|
|» » » » » percentage|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» » » » amountNet|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The net total cost, i.e. excluding VAT|
|» » » » amountVat|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|The applicable VAT|
|» » » » amountGross|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The gross total cost, i.e. including VAT|
|» » » revenue|[object]|false|none|An array of revenue objects containing the total revenue for each payment method during this period.|
|» » » » description|string|true|none|A description of the revenue subtotal|
|» » » » method|[settlement-method](#schemasettlement-method)|true|none|The method the cost or revenue subtotal applies to. This is usually a payment method, but can also represent a<br>correction or transaction type that is not tied to a specific payment method.|
|» » » » count|integer|true|none|The number of payments|
|» » » » amountNet|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The net total of received funds, i.e. excluding VAT|
|» » » » amountVat|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|The applicable VAT|
|» » » » amountGross|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The gross total of received funds, i.e. including VAT|
|» » » invoiceId|[invoiceToken](#schemainvoicetoken)|false|none|The ID of the invoice created for this period, if the invoice has been created already.|
|» » » invoiceReference|string \| null|false|none|The invoice reference, if the invoice has been created already.|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|
|id|[open-settlement-id](#schemaopen-settlement-id)|true|read-only|none|
|_links|[settlement-convenience-links](#schemasettlement-convenience-links)|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.<br><br>This endpoint always points to your organization's current open or next settlement rather than one specific<br>settlement, so it doesn't return links to that settlement's payments, captures, refunds, chargebacks, or invoice.|

## Get next settlement

<a id="opIdget-next-settlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/settlements/next \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/settlements/next`

Retrieve the details of the current settlement, that has not yet been paid out.

For a complete reference of the settlement object, refer to the [Get settlement endpoint](get-settlement)
documentation.

For more accurate bookkeeping, refer to the [balance report](get-balance-report) endpoint or the
[balance transactions](list-balance-transactions) endpoint.

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit has been reached.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<h3 id="get-next-settlement-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a settlement object. Will always contain the string `settlement` for this<br>endpoint.|
|id|string|true|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this settlement.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|reference|string \| null|false|read-only|The settlement's bank reference, as found in your Mollie account and on your bank statement.|
|settledAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date on which the settlement was settled, in ISO 8601 format.<br><br>For an [open settlement](get-open-settlement) or for the [next settlement](get-next-settlement), no settlement<br>date is available.|
|status|object|true|read-only|none|
|amount|object|true|read-only|none|
|» currency|string|true|none|A three-character ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» value|string|true|none|A string containing an exact monetary amount in the given currency.|
|balanceId|object|true|read-only|The balance token that the settlement was settled to.|
|invoiceId|string \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the oldest invoice created for all the periods, if the invoice has been created yet.|
|periods|object|false|read-only|For bookkeeping purposes, the settlement includes an overview of transactions included in the settlement. These<br>transactions are grouped into 'period' objects — one for each calendar month.<br><br>For example, if a settlement includes funds from 15 April until 4 May, it will include two period objects. One for<br>all transactions processed between 15 April and 30 April, and one for all transactions between 1 May and 4 May.<br><br>Period objects are grouped by year, and then by month. So in the above example, the full `periods` collection will<br>look as follows: `{"2024": {"04": {...}, "05": {...}}}`. The year and month in this documentation are referred as `<year>` and `<month>`.<br><br>The example response should give a good idea of what this looks like in practise.|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » costs|[object]|false|none|An array of cost objects, describing the fees withheld for each payment method during this period.|
|» » » » description|string|true|none|A description of the cost subtotal|
|» » » » method|[settlement-method](#schemasettlement-method)|true|none|The method the cost or revenue subtotal applies to. This is usually a payment method, but can also represent a<br>correction or transaction type that is not tied to a specific payment method.|
|» » » » count|integer|true|none|The number of fees|
|» » » » rate|object|true|none|The service rates, further divided into `fixed` and `percentage` costs.<br><br>For pass-through fees, which are charged by an external party rather than at an agreed Mollie<br>rate, both `fixed` and `percentage` are `null`.|
|» » » » » fixed|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|In v2 endpoints, monetary amounts are represented as objects with a `currency` and `value` field.|
|» » » » » percentage|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» » » » amountNet|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The net total cost, i.e. excluding VAT|
|» » » » amountVat|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|The applicable VAT|
|» » » » amountGross|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The gross total cost, i.e. including VAT|
|» » » revenue|[object]|false|none|An array of revenue objects containing the total revenue for each payment method during this period.|
|» » » » description|string|true|none|A description of the revenue subtotal|
|» » » » method|[settlement-method](#schemasettlement-method)|true|none|The method the cost or revenue subtotal applies to. This is usually a payment method, but can also represent a<br>correction or transaction type that is not tied to a specific payment method.|
|» » » » count|integer|true|none|The number of payments|
|» » » » amountNet|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The net total of received funds, i.e. excluding VAT|
|» » » » amountVat|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|true|none|The applicable VAT|
|» » » » amountGross|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The gross total of received funds, i.e. including VAT|
|» » » invoiceId|[invoiceToken](#schemainvoicetoken)|false|none|The ID of the invoice created for this period, if the invoice has been created already.|
|» » » invoiceReference|string \| null|false|none|The invoice reference, if the invoice has been created already.|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|
|id|[next-settlement-id](#schemanext-settlement-id)|true|read-only|none|
|_links|[settlement-convenience-links](#schemasettlement-convenience-links)|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.<br><br>This endpoint always points to your organization's current open or next settlement rather than one specific<br>settlement, so it doesn't return links to that settlement's payments, captures, refunds, chargebacks, or invoice.|

## List settlement payments

<a id="opIdlist-settlement-payments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/settlements/stl_5B8cwPMGnU/payments \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/settlements/{settlementId}/payments`

Retrieve all payments included in the given settlement.

The response is in the same format as the response of the [List payments endpoint](list-payments).

For capture-based payment methods such as Klarna, the payments are not listed here. Refer to the
[List captures endpoint](list-captures) endpoint instead.

<h3 id="list-settlement-payments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|[paymentToken](#schemapaymenttoken)|false|Provide an ID to start the result set from the item with the given ID and onwards. This allows you to paginate<br>the result set.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50 items.|
|sort|query|[sorting](#schemasorting)|false|Used for setting the direction of the result set. Defaults to descending order, meaning the results are ordered from<br>newest to oldest.|
|profileId|query|[profileToken](#schemaprofiletoken)|false|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) you wish to<br>retrieve the resources for.<br><br>Most API credentials are linked to a single profile. In these cases the `profileId` must not be sent. For<br>organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens however, the `profileId` parameter is required.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|settlementId|path|[settlementToken](#schemasettlementtoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related settlement.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

<h3 id="list-settlement-payments-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|[list-count](#schemalist-count)|true|none|The number of items in this result set. If more items are available, a `_links.next` URL will be present in the result<br>as well.<br><br>The maximum number of items per result set is controlled by the `limit` property provided in the request. The default<br>limit is 50 items.|
|_embedded|object|true|none|none|
|» payments|[[list-settlement-payment-response](#schemalist-settlement-payment-response)]|false|none|An array of payment objects.|
|_links|[list-links](#schemalist-links)|true|none|Links to help navigate through the lists of items. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

`GET /v2/settlements/{settlementId}/refunds`

|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

## Create subscription

<a id="opIdcreate-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/customers/cst_5B8cwPMGnU/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "times": 6,
    "interval": "2 days",
    "startDate": "2025-01-01",
    "description": "Subscription of streaming channel",
    "method": "paypal",
    "applicationFee": {
      "amount": {
        "currency": "EUR",
        "value": "10.00"
      },
      "description": "Platform fee"
    },
    "metadata": "string",
    "webhookUrl": "https://example.com/webhook",
    "mandateId": "mdt_5B8cwPMGnU",
    "profileId": {},
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/customers/{customerId}/subscriptions`

With subscriptions, you can schedule recurring payments to take place at regular intervals.

For example, by simply specifying an `amount` and an `interval`, you can create an endless subscription to charge a
monthly fee, until you cancel the subscription.

Or, you could use the times parameter to only charge a limited number of times, for example to split a big
transaction in multiple parts.

A few example usages:

`amount[currency]="EUR"` `amount[value]="5.00"` `interval="2 weeks"`
Your customer will be charged €5 once every two weeks.

`amount[currency]="EUR"` `amount[value]="20.00"` `interval="1 day" times=5`
Your customer will be charged €20 every day, for five consecutive days.

`amount[currency]="EUR"` `amount[value]="10.00"` `interval="1 month"`
`startDate="2018-04-30"`
Your customer will be charged €10 on the last day of each month, starting in April 2018.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "times": 6,
  "interval": "2 days",
  "startDate": "2025-01-01",
  "description": "Subscription of streaming channel",
  "method": "paypal",
  "applicationFee": {
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "description": "Platform fee"
  },
  "metadata": "string",
  "webhookUrl": "https://example.com/webhook",
  "mandateId": "mdt_5B8cwPMGnU",
  "profileId": {},
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|customerId|path|[customerToken](#schemacustomertoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related customer.|
|body|body|[subscription-request](#schemasubscription-request)|false|none|
|» amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|The amount for each individual payment that is charged with this subscription. For example, for a monthly<br>subscription of €10, the subscription amount should be set to €10.|
|» times|body|integer \| null|false|Total number of payments for the subscription. Once this number of payments is reached, the subscription is<br>considered completed.<br><br>Test mode subscriptions will get canceled automatically after 10 payments.|
|» interval|body|string|false|Interval to wait between payments, for example `1 month` or `14 days`.<br><br>The maximum interval is one year (`12 months`, `52 weeks`, or `365 days`).<br><br>Possible values: `... days`, `... weeks`, `... months`.|
|» startDate|body|string|false|The start date of the subscription in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.|
|» description|body|string|false|The subscription's description will be used as the description of the resulting individual payments and so showing<br>up on the bank statement of the consumer.<br><br>**Please note:** the description needs to be unique for the Customer in case it has multiple active subscriptions.|
|» method|body|[subscription-method](#schemasubscription-method)|false|The payment method used for this subscription. If omitted, any of the customer's valid mandates may be used.|
|» applicationFee|body|object|false|With Mollie Connect you can charge fees on payments that your app is processing on behalf of other Mollie<br>merchants.<br><br>Setting an application fee on the subscription will ensure this fee is charged on each individual payment.<br><br>Refer to the `applicationFee` parameter on the [Get payment endpoint](get-payment) documentation for more<br>information.|
|» » amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|In v2 endpoints, monetary amounts are represented as objects with a `currency` and `value` field.|
|» » description|body|string|true|none|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Provide any data you like, for example a string or a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity.<br>Whenever you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately<br>1kB.<br><br>Any metadata added to the subscription will be automatically forwarded to the payments generated for it.|
|» webhookUrl|body|string \| null|false|We will call this URL for any payment status changes of payments resulting from this subscription.<br><br>This webhook will receive **all** events for the subscription's payments. This may include payment failures as<br>well. Be sure to verify the payment's subscription ID and its status.|
|» mandateId|body|[mandateToken](#schemamandatetoken)|false|The mandate used for this subscription, if any.|
|» profileId|body|object|false|none|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» method|creditcard|
|» method|directdebit|
|» method|paypal|
|» method|null|

## Update subscription

<a id="opIdupdate-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/customers/cst_5B8cwPMGnU/subscriptions/sub_5B8cwPMGnU \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "description": "Subscription of streaming channel",
    "interval": "1 months",
    "startDate": "2025-01-01",
    "times": 6,
    "metadata": "string",
    "webhookUrl": "https://example.com/webhook",
    "mandateId": "mdt_5B8cwPMGnU",
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/customers/{customerId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

Update an existing subscription.

Canceled subscriptions cannot be updated.

For an in-depth explanation of each parameter, refer to the [Create subscription](create-subscription) endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "description": "Subscription of streaming channel",
  "interval": "1 months",
  "startDate": "2025-01-01",
  "times": 6,
  "metadata": "string",
  "webhookUrl": "https://example.com/webhook",
  "mandateId": "mdt_5B8cwPMGnU",
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|customerId|path|[customerToken](#schemacustomertoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related customer.|
|subscriptionId|path|[subscriptionToken](#schemasubscriptiontoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related subscription.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|Update the amount for future payments of this subscription.|
|» description|body|string|false|The subscription's description will be used as the description of the resulting individual payments and so showing<br>up on the bank statement of the consumer.<br><br>**Please note:** the description needs to be unique for the Customer in case it has multiple active subscriptions.|
|» interval|body|string|false|Interval to wait between payments, for example `1 month` or `14 days`.<br><br>The maximum interval is one year (`12 months`, `52 weeks`, or `365 days`).<br><br>Possible values: `... days`, `... weeks`, `... months`.|
|» startDate|body|string|false|The start date of the subscription in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.|
|» times|body|integer|false|Total number of payments for the subscription. Once this number of payments is reached, the subscription is<br>considered completed.<br><br>Test mode subscriptions will get canceled automatically after 10 payments.|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Provide any data you like, for example a string or a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the<br>entity. Whenever you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to<br>approximately 1kB.<br><br>Any metadata added to the subscription will be automatically forwarded to the payments generated for it.|
|» webhookUrl|body|string|false|We will call this URL for any payment status changes of payments resulting from this subscription.<br><br>This webhook will receive **all** events for the subscription's payments. This may include payment<br>failures as well. Be sure to verify the payment's subscription ID and its status.|
|» mandateId|body|[mandateToken](#schemamandatetoken)|false|The mandate used for this subscription, if any.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-patch](#schematestmode-patch)|false|Whether the entity was created in test mode or live mode. This field does not update the mode of the entity.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

> Example responses

## List terminal pairing codes

<a id="opIdterminals-list-pairing-codes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/terminals/pairing-codes \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/terminals/pairing-codes`

> ℹ️ **Test mode**
>
> This endpoint currently does not support test mode yet.

Returns your pairing codes: `active`, `expired`, and `revoked`. Results are paginated.

We keep a pairing code for one month after it is revoked or expires, then delete it. Deleted codes drop out of
this list. Active pairing codes are never deleted.

<h3 id="list-terminal-pairing-codes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string \| null|false|Provide an ID to start the result set from the item with the given ID and onwards. This allows you to paginate the<br>result set.|
|limit|query|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50 items.|
|sort|query|[sorting](#schemasorting)|false|Used for setting the direction of the result set. Defaults to descending order, meaning the results are ordered from<br>newest to oldest.|
|profileId|query|string|false|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) you wish to retrieve pairing codes for.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|

## Request terminal pairing code

<a id="opIdterminals-request-pairing-code"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/terminals/pairing-codes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "profileId": "pfl_jA9bC4DkFj3G"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/terminals/pairing-codes`

> ℹ️ **Test mode**
>
> This endpoint currently does not support test mode yet.

Request a pairing code to onboard a point-of-sale terminal.

The response includes a human-readable `code` for manual entry on the terminal, and a QR Code as a
base64 encoded SVG data URI for scanning if you specify the query parameter `include` with value `details.qrCode`.

Pairing codes expire after 90 days (see `expiresAt`) and can be used multiple times.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "profileId": "pfl_jA9bC4DkFj3G"
}
```

<h3 id="request-terminal-pairing-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|string \| null|false|This endpoint allows you to include additional information via the `include` query string parameter.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» profileId|body|string|true|The ID of the profile to pair the terminal with.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json

  "resource": "terminal-pairing-code",
  "id": "termpc_R7gX5Ea9bC4DkFj3G",
  "mode": "live",
  "code": "20eb5ca1f78b48ae9e2b",
  "profileId": "pfl_jA9bC4DkFj3G",
  "status": "active",
  "details": {
    "qrCode": {
      "height": 256,
      "width": 256,
      "src": "data:image/svg+xml;base64,PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4w...IzAwMDAwMCIvPjwvZz48L2c+PC9zdmc+Cg=="
    }
  },
  "expiresAt": "2026-03-10T10:00:00+00:00",
  "revokedAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2025-12-10T10:00:00+00:00",
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "https://api.mollie.com/v2/terminals/pairing-codes/termpc_R7gX5Ea9bC4DkFj3G?include=details.qrCode",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "profile": {

      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://docs.mollie.com/reference/terminals-request-pairing-code",

    }
  }
}
```

## Revoke terminal pairing code

<a id="opIdterminals-revoke-pairing-code"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/terminals/pairing-codes/termpc_R7gX5Ea9bC4DkFj3G \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \

```

`DELETE /v2/terminals/pairing-codes/{pairingCodeId}`

> ℹ️ **Test mode**
>
> This endpoint currently does not support test mode yet.

Revoke a pairing code, preventing the onboarding of new point-of-sale terminals.

Terminals that have already paired with this code are not affected.

We keep a revoked pairing code for one month, then delete it. Once deleted, this endpoint returns a 404.

<h3 id="revoke-terminal-pairing-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|

## Create transfer

<a id="opIdcreate-transfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/business-accounts/transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Client-Signature: string' \
  -H 'X-Client-Signed-At: 2025-01-01T12:00:00Z' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 12345678-abcd' \
  -d '{
    "debtorIban": "NL55MLLE0123456789",
    "creditor": {
      "fullName": "Jan Jansen",
      "account": {
        "iban": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
      }
    },
    "amount": {
      "currency": "EUR",
      "value": "10.00"
    },
    "description": "Invoice 12345",
    "transferScheme": {
      "type": "sepa-credit-inst"
    },
    "metadata": "string",
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/business-accounts/transfers`

> 🚧 Beta feature
>
> This feature is currently in beta testing, and the final specification may still change.

Create a SEPA Credit Transfer from your Mollie Business Account.

To initiate a transfer, you must provide the transfer scheme, the amount, the debtor IBAN (your Mollie Business
Account IBAN), and the creditor (recipient) details.

Each request must include an `Idempotency-Key` header to prevent duplicate transfers, and must be signed using the
`X-Client-Signature` and `X-Client-Signed-At` headers.

### Simulating transfer scenarios in test mode

In test mode, you can simulate various transfer scenarios by adjusting the transfer amount. This allows you to
mimic the typical status progression of a real-world transfer. Note that a transfer's progression will stop once
it reaches a final status: `blocked`, `failed`, `processed`, or `returned`.

| Amount  | Scenario                                            | Webhook sequence                                                                                                                                                   |
|---------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `11.00` | Transfer initiated, pending review by Mollie        | `business-account-transfer.requested` → `business-account-transfer.initiated` → `business-account-transfer.pending-review`                                         |
| `12.00` | Transfer initiated, blocked by Mollie               | `business-account-transfer.requested` → `business-account-transfer.initiated` → `business-account-transfer.pending-review` → `business-account-transfer.blocked`   |
| `13.00` | Transfer initiated, failed on scheme submission     | `business-account-transfer.requested` → `business-account-transfer.initiated` → `business-account-transfer.failed`                                                 |
| `14.00` | Transfer processed, then returned by receiving bank | `business-account-transfer.requested` → `business-account-transfer.initiated` → `business-account-transfer.processed` → `business-account-transfer.returned`       |
| Other   | Default: transfer is processed                      | `business-account-transfer.requested` → `business-account-transfer.initiated` → `business-account-transfer.processed`                                              |

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "debtorIban": "NL55MLLE0123456789",
  "creditor": {
    "fullName": "Jan Jansen",
    "account": {
      "iban": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
    }
  },
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "description": "Invoice 12345",
  "transferScheme": {
    "type": "sepa-credit-inst"
  },
  "metadata": "string",
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Client-Signature|header|string|true|A cryptographic signature of the request payload, used to verify the authenticity of the transfer request.|
|X-Client-Signed-At|header|string|true|The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the client signed the request. Used in conjunction with<br>`X-Client-Signature` for request verification.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|true|A unique value used to identify this request and prevent duplicate transfers. UUIDv4 is recommended to<br>guarantee uniqueness across multiple processes or servers. If two requests are received with the same<br>idempotency key, the second request will be discarded.<br><br>View the [public documentation](https://docs.mollie.com/reference/api-idempotency#using-an-idempotency-key)<br>to learn more.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[transfer-request](#schematransfer-request)|false|none|
|» debtorIban|body|string|true|The IBAN of the debtor's (sender) Mollie account from which to initiate the transfer.|
|» creditor|body|[transfer-party](#schematransfer-party)|true|The creditor (recipient) of the transfer, including their name and account details.|
|» amount|body|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|The amount of the transfer, e.g. `{"currency":"EUR", "value":"100.00"}` if you would want to transfer €100.00.<br><br>Only `EUR` is supported for SEPA transfers.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|A short description of the transfer. This will appear on the bank statement of both the debtor and creditor.<br><br>It must begin with an alphanumeric character, followed by any combination of letters, numbers, spaces or special characters `/ - ? : ( ) . , ' + _`.<br><br>Constraints:<br>- Cannot be solely a hyphen (-) or colon (:)<br>- Cannot contain consecutive hyphens (--)<br>- Cannot contain consecutive colons (::)|
|» transferScheme|body|[transfer-scheme](#schematransfer-scheme)|true|The scheme, as requested by the client.|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Provide any data you like, for example a string or a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity. Whenever<br>you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately 1kB.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": "batrf_87GByBuj4UCcUTEbs6aGJ",
  "mode": "live",
  "businessAccountTransactionId": "batr_87GByBuj4UCcUTEbs6aGJ",

  },
```
