<h1 id="mollie-api-verify-payee-api">Verify Payee API</h1>

Operations related to the Verify Payee API

## Verify Payee

<a id="opIdverify-payee"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/business-accounts/payee-verifications \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "creditorBankAccount": {
      "accountHolderName": "Jan Jansen",
      "format": "iban",
      "accountNumber": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
    },
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/business-accounts/payee-verifications`

> 🚧 Beta feature
>
> This feature is currently in beta testing, and the final specification may still change.

Perform a Verification of Payee (VoP) check. This allows you to verify the account holder name against the
records held by the receiving bank before initiating a transfer.

The verification result indicates whether the provided name matches, closely matches, or does not match the
name on file at the receiving bank. This helps prevent misdirected payments.

### Simulating verification scenarios in test mode

In test mode, you can simulate various verification outcomes by adjusting the creditor name in the
`creditorBankAccount.accountHolderName` property. This allows you to test all possible Verification of Payee
results without needing special properties. The names are case insensitive.

| Account holder name                    | Scenario                                      | Verification result | Suggested name |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| `John Close Match`                     | Name closely matches the bank records          | `close-match`       | `John Match`   |
| `John No Match`                        | Name does not match the bank records           | `no-match`          | —              |
| `John Unavailable`                     | Verification is not available                  | `not-available`     | —              |
| Any other name                         | Default: name matches the bank records         | `match`             | —              |

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "creditorBankAccount": {
    "accountHolderName": "Jan Jansen",
    "format": "iban",
    "accountNumber": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
  },
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="verify-payee-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|[verification-of-payee-request](#schemaverification-of-payee-request)|false|none|
|» creditorBankAccount|body|[creditor-bank-account](#schemacreditor-bank-account)|true|The bank account details of the creditor (recipient) to verify.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "resource": "business-account-payee-verification",
  "mode": "live",
  "creditorBankAccount": {
    "accountHolderName": "Jan Jansen",
    "format": "iban",
    "accountNumber": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
  },
  "verificationResult": {
    "outcome": "match"
  },
  "createdAt": "2025-01-01T12:00:00+00:00"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "status": 422,
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "detail": "The 'creditorBankAccount.accountNumber' field is missing",
  "field": "creditorBankAccount.accountNumber",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://docs.mollie.com/overview/handling-errors",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

<h1 id="mollie-api-wallets-api">Wallets API</h1>

Operations related to the Wallets API

## Request Apple Pay payment session

<a id="opIdrequest-apple-pay-payment-session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/wallets/applepay/sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "validationUrl": "https://apple-pay-gateway-cert.apple.com/paymentservices/paymentSession",
    "domain": "pay.myshop.com",
    "profileId": "pfl_5B8cwPMGnU"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/wallets/applepay/sessions`

When integrating Apple Pay in your own checkout on the web, you need to
[provide merchant validation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/apple_pay_js_api/providing_merchant_validation).
This is normally done using Apple's
[Requesting an Apple Pay Session](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/apple_pay_js_api/requesting_an_apple_pay_payment_session).
The merchant validation proves to Apple that a validated merchant is calling the Apple Pay Javascript APIs.

To integrate Apple Pay via Mollie, you will have to call the Mollie API instead of Apple's API. The response of this
API call can then be passed as-is to the completion method, `completeMerchantValidation`.

Before requesting an Apple Pay Payment Session, you must place the domain validation file on your server at:
`https://[domain]/.well-known/apple-developer-merchantid-domain-association`. Without this file, it will not be
possible to use Apple Pay on your domain.

Each new transaction requires a new payment session object. Merchant session objects are not reusable, and they
expire after five minutes.

Payment sessions cannot be requested directly from the browser. The request must be sent from your server. For the
full documentation, see the official
[Apple Pay JS API](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/apple_pay_js_api) documentation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "validationUrl": "https://apple-pay-gateway-cert.apple.com/paymentservices/paymentSession",
  "domain": "pay.myshop.com",
  "profileId": "pfl_5B8cwPMGnU"
}
```

<h3 id="request-apple-pay-payment-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» validationUrl|body|string|true|The validationUrl you got from the<br>[ApplePayValidateMerchant event](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/applepayvalidatemerchantevent).<br><br>A list of all<br>[valid host names](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple_pay_on_the_web/setting_up_your_server)<br>for merchant validation is available. You should white list these in your application and reject any<br>`validationUrl`s that have a host name not in the list.|
|» domain|body|string|true|The domain of your web shop, that is visible in the browser's location bar. For example<br>`pay.myshop.com`.|
|» profileId|body|[profileToken](#schemaprofiletoken)|false|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) this entity belongs to.<br><br>Most API credentials are linked to a single profile. In these cases the `profileId` must not be sent in<br>the creation request. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens however, the<br>`profileId` parameter is required.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "epochTimestamp": 1555507053169,
  "expiresAt": 1555510653169,
  "merchantSessionIdentifier": "SSH2EAF8AFAEAA94DEEA898162A5DAFD36E_916523AAED1343F5BC5815E12BEE9250AFFDC1A17C46B0DE5A9",
  "nonce": "0206b8db",
  "merchantIdentifier": "BD62FEB196874511C22DB28A9E14A89E3534C93194F73EA417EC566368D391EB",
  "domainName": "pay.example.org",
  "displayName": "Chuck Norris's Store",
  "signature": "308006092a864886f7...8cc030ad3000000000000"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "status": 422,
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "detail": "Apple is not able to verify your domain",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

  "status": 429,

  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
```

`GET /v2/webhooks`

Returns a paginated list of your webhooks. If no webhook endpoints are available, the resulting array will be empty. This request should never throw an error.

<h3 id="list-all-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Create a webhook

<a id="opIdcreate-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Webhook #1",
    "url": "https://mollie.com/",
    "eventTypes": [
      "payment-link.paid"
    ],
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/webhooks`

A webhook must have a name, an url and a list of event types. You can also create webhooks in the webhooks settings section of the Dashboard.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Webhook #1",
  "url": "https://mollie.com/",
  "eventTypes": [
    "payment-link.paid"
  ],
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A name that identifies the webhook.|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL Mollie will send the events to. This URL must be publicly accessible.|
|» eventTypes|body|[[webhook-event-types](#schemawebhook-event-types)] \| [webhook-event-types](#schemawebhook-event-types)|true|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[webhook-event-types](#schemawebhook-event-types)]|false|The list of events to enable for this webhook. You may specify `'*'` to add all events, except those<br>that require explicit selection.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[webhook-event-types](#schemawebhook-event-types)|false|The list of events to enable for this webhook. You may specify `'*'` to add all events, except those<br>that require explicit selection.|
|» testmode|body|[oauth-testmode-create](#schemaoauth-testmode-create)|false|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>You can enable test mode by setting `testmode` to `true`.|

## Get a webhook

## Update a webhook

<a id="opIdupdate-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/webhooks/hook_1234567890 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Webhook #1",
    "url": "https://mollie.com/",
    "eventTypes": [
      "payment-link.paid"
    ],
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Updates the webhook. You may edit the name, url and the list of subscribed event types.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Webhook #1",
  "url": "https://mollie.com/",
  "eventTypes": [
    "payment-link.paid"
  ],
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|webhookId|path|[webhookToken](#schemawebhooktoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related webhook.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A name that identifies the webhook.|

|» » *oneOf*|body|[webhook-event-types](#schemawebhook-event-types)|false|The list of events to enable for this webhook. You may specify `'*'` to add all events, except those<br>that require explicit selection.|
|» testmode|body|[testmode-patch](#schematestmode-patch)|false|Whether the entity was created in test mode or live mode. This field does not update the mode of the entity.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. ## Test a webhook

<a id="opIdtest-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.mollie.com/v2/webhooks/hook_1234567890/ping \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/hal+json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "testmode": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}/ping`

Sends a test event to the webhook to verify the endpoint is working as expected.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "testmode": false
}
```

<h3 id="test-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique key to ensure idempotent requests. This key should be a UUID v4 string.|
|webhookId|path|[webhookToken](#schemawebhooktoken)|true|Provide the ID of the related webhook.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» testmode|body|[oauth-testmode](#schemaoauth-testmode)|false|You can enable test mode by setting `testmode` to `true`.<br><br>Test entities cannot be retrieved when the endpoint is set to live mode, and vice versa.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "status": 404,
  "title": "Not Found",
  "detail": "No entity exists with token 'uct_abcDEFghij123456789'",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "status": 422,
  "title": "Unprocessable entity",
  "detail": "This subscription was already deleted.",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "...",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "detail": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please slow down your requests.",
  "_links": {
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://docs.mollie.com/overview/handling-errors",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="test-a-webhook-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted.|None|
|404|Not Found|No entity with this ID exists.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request contains issues. For example, if the webhook has already been deleted.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate Limit has been reached.|[error-response](#schemaerror-response)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a balance report object. Will always contain the string `balance-report` for this<br>endpoint.|
|balanceId|[balanceToken](#schemabalancetoken)|true|none|The ID of the balance this report is generated for.|
|timeZone|string|true|none|The time zone used for the from and until parameters. Currently only time zone `Europe/Amsterdam` is supported.|
|from|string|true|none|The start date of the report, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. The from date is 'inclusive', and in Central European Time.<br>This means a report with for example `from=2024-01-01` will include movements of 2024-01-01 00:00:00 CET and<br>onwards.|
|until|string|true|none|The end date of the report, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. The until date is 'exclusive', and in Central European Time.<br>This means a report with for example `until=2024-02-01` will include movements up until 2024-01-31 23:59:59 CET.|
|grouping|[balance-report-grouping](#schemabalance-report-grouping)|true|none|none|
|totals|object|true|none|Totals are grouped according to the chosen grouping rule. The example response should give a good idea of what a<br>typical grouping looks like.<br><br>If grouping `status-balances` is chosen, the main grouping is as follows:<br><br>* `pendingBalance` containing an `open`, `pending`, `movedToAvailable`, and `close` sub-group<br>* `availableBalance` containing an `open`, `movedFromPending`, `immediatelyAvailable`, and `close` sub-group<br><br>If grouping `transaction-categories` is chosen, the main grouping is as follows:<br><br>* `open` and `close` groups, each containing a `pending` and `available` sub-group<br>* Transaction type groups such as `payments`, `refunds`, `chargebacks`, `capital`, `transfers`, `fee-prepayments`, `corrections`, `topups`<br>each containing a `pending`, `movedToAvailable`, and<br>`immediatelyAvailable` sub-group<br><br>Each sub-group typically has:<br><br>* An `amount` object containing the group's total amount<br>* A `count` integer if relevant (for example, counting the number of refunds)<br>* A `subtotals` array containing more sub-group objects if applicable|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|grouping|status-balances|
|grouping|transaction-categories|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a balance transaction object. Will always contain the string `balance-transaction`<br>for this endpoint.|
|id|object|true|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this balance transaction.|
|type|[balance-transaction-type](#schemabalance-transaction-type)|true|none|The type of transaction, for example `payment` or `refund`. Values include the below examples, although this list<br>is not definitive.<br><br>* Regular payment processing: `payment` `capture` `unauthorized-direct-debit` `failed-payment`<br>* Refunds and chargebacks: `refund` `returned-refund` `chargeback` `chargeback-reversal`<br>* Settlements: `outgoing-transfer` `canceled-outgoing-transfer` `returned-transfer`<br>* Invoicing: `invoice-compensation` `balance-correction`<br>* Mollie Connect: `application-fee` `split-payment` `platform-payment-refund` `platform-payment-chargeback`|
|resultAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The final amount that was moved to or from the balance. If the transaction moves funds away from the balance, for<br>example when it concerns a refund, the amount will be negative.|
|initialAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The amount that was to be moved to or from the balance, excluding deductions. If the transaction moves funds away<br>from the balance, for example when it concerns a refund, the amount will be negative.|
|deductions|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|false|none|The total amount of deductions withheld from the movement. For example, if we charge a €0.29 fee on a €10 payment,<br>the deductions amount will be `{"currency":"EUR", "value":"-0.29"}`.<br><br>When moving funds to a balance, we always round the deduction to a 'real' amount. Any differences between these<br>real-time rounded amounts and the final invoice will be compensated when the invoice is generated.|
|deductionDetails|object \| null|false|none|A detailed breakdown of the deductions withheld from the movement. Each field represents a specific type of<br>deduction applied to the transaction. Only the applicable fields will be present.|
|context|object \| null|false|none|Depending on the type of the balance transaction, we will try to give more context about the specific event that<br>triggered it. For example, the context object for a payment transaction will look like<br>`{"paymentId": "tr_5B8cwPMGnU6qLbRvo7qEZo", "paymentDescription": "Description"}`.<br><br>Below is a complete list of the context values that each type of transaction will have.<br><br>* Type `payment`: `paymentId`, `paymentDescription`<br>* Type `capture`: `paymentId` `captureId`, `paymentDescription`, `captureDescription`<br>* Type `capture-commission`: `paymentId`, `paymentDescription`, `organizationId`<br>* Type `capture-rolling-reserve-release`: `paymentId`, `paymentDescription`, `captureId`,   "reportType": "transaction_margin",
```json
  "fromDate": "2026-08-01",
  "untilDate": "2026-08-31"
}
```

Generate a transaction margin report for your organization over a date range.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reportType|[report-type](#schemareport-type)|true|none|The type of report to generate. Determines which other fields the request needs, and which fields show up<br>on the resulting report.|
|fromDate|string(date)|true|none|The start date of the report period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Must be strictly before `untilDate`; a<br>report can't cover a single day. Data is available from 2026-01-01 onwards.|
|untilDate|string(date)|true|none|The end date of the report period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Must be strictly after `fromDate`.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reportType|transaction_margin|

```json
{
  "resource": "report",
  "id": {},

  "fromDate": "2026-08-01",
  "untilDate": "2026-08-31",
  "status": {},
  "statusReason": {
    "code": "generation_failed",
    "message": "Something went wrong while generating the report. Try again, or contact support if it keeps happening."
  },
  "createdAt": "2024-03-20T09:13:37+00:00",
  "completedAt": "2026-09-01T09:01:12+00:00",
  "failedAt": "2026-09-01T09:03:00+00:00",
  "downloadExpiresAt": "2026-09-01T09:16:12+00:00",
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "https://...",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "download": {
      "href": "https://...",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    },
    "documentation": {
      "href": "https://...",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a report object. Will always contain the string `report` for this<br>endpoint.|
|id|object|true|read-only|none|
|reportType|[report-type-response](#schemareport-type-response)|true|none|The type of report to generate. Determines which other fields the request needs, and which fields show up<br>on the resulting report.|
|fromDate|string \| null(date)|false|read-only|The start date of the report period. Set for date-range report types, `null` otherwise.|
|untilDate|string \| null(date)|false|read-only|The end date of the report period. Set for date-range report types, `null` otherwise.|
|status|object|true|read-only|none|
|statusReason|[report-status-reason](#schemareport-status-reason)|false|read-only|Present when `status` is `failed`. Explains what went wrong.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|true|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|completedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time the report finished generating, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format. Only present once `status` is `completed`.|
|failedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time the report failed to generate, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format. Only present once `status` is `failed`.|
|downloadExpiresAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time the `_links.download` link expires, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format. We issue a fresh link and expiry on every call to [Get report](get-report), so just call it<br>again once this one expires.|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reportType|transaction_margin|

These<br>transactions are grouped into 'period' objects — one for each calendar month.<br><br>For example, if a settlement includes funds from 15 April until 4 May, it will include two period objects. One for<br>all transactions processed between 15 April and 30 April, and one for all transactions between 1 May and 4 May.<br><br>Period objects are grouped by year, and then by month. So in the above example, the full `periods` collection will<br>look as follows: `{"2024": {"04": {...}, "05": {...}}}`. The year and month in this documentation are referred as `<year>` and `<month>`.<br><br>The example response should give a good idea of what this looks like in practise.|

|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|reference|string \| null|false|read-only|The settlement's bank reference, as found in your Mollie account and on your bank statement.|
|settledAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date on which the settlement was settled, in ISO 8601 format.<br><br>For an [open settlement](get-open-settlement) or for the [next settlement](get-next-settlement), no settlement<br>date is available.|
|status|object|true|read-only|none|
|amount|object|true|read-only|none|
|balanceId|object|true|read-only|The balance token that the settlement was settled to.|
|invoiceId|string \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the oldest invoice created for all the periods, if the invoice has been created yet.|
|periods|object|false|read-only|For bookkeeping purposes, the settlement includes an overview of transactions included in the settlement. These<br>transactions are grouped into 'period' objects — one for each calendar month.<br><br>For example, if a settlement includes funds from 15 April until 4 May, it will include two period objects. One for<br>all transactions processed between 15 April and 30 April, and one for all transactions between 1 May and 4 May.<br><br>Period objects are grouped by year, and then by month. So in the above example, the full `periods` collection will<br>look as follows: `{"2024": {"04": {...}, "05": {...}}}`. The year and month in this documentation are referred as `<year>` and `<month>`.<br><br>The example response should give a good idea of what this looks like in practise.|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|
|id|[settlement-id](#schemasettlement-id)|true|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this settlement.|
|_links|[settlement-links](#schemasettlement-links)|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.

This endpoint always points to your organization's current open or next settlement rather than one specific
settlement, so it doesn't return links to that settlement's payments, captures, refunds, chargebacks, or invoice.

<h2 id="tocS_payment-line-item">payment-line-item</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocspayment-line-item"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "physical",
  "description": "LEGO 4440 Forest Police Station",
  "quantity": 1,
  "quantityUnit": "pcs",
  "unitPrice": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "discountAmount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "totalAmount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "vatRate": "21.00",
  "vatAmount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "sku": "9780241661628",
  "categories": [
    "meal",
    "eco"
  ],
  "imageUrl": "https://...",
  "productUrl": "https://..."
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|[payment-line-type](#schemapayment-line-type)|false|none|The type of product purchased. For example, a physical or a digital product.<br><br>The `tip` payment line type is not available when creating a payment.|
|description|string|true|none|A description of the line item. For example *LEGO 4440 Forest Police Station*.|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The number of items.|
|quantityUnit|string|false|none|The unit for the quantity. For example *pcs*, *kg*, or *cm*.|
|unitPrice|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The price of a single item including VAT.<br><br>For example: `{"currency":"EUR", "value":"89.00"}` if the box of LEGO costs €89.00 each.<br><br>For types `discount`, `store_credit`, and `gift_card`, the unit price must be negative.<br><br>The unit price can be zero in case of free items.|
|discountAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|Any line-specific discounts, as a positive amount. Not relevant if the line itself is already a discount<br>type.|
|totalAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The total amount of the line, including VAT and discounts.<br><br>Should match the following formula: `(unitPrice × quantity) - discountAmount`.<br><br>The sum of all `totalAmount` values of all order lines should be equal to the full payment amount.|
|vatRate|string|false|none|The VAT rate applied to the line, for example `21.00` for 21%. The vatRate should be passed as a string and<br>not as a float, to ensure the correct number of decimals are passed.|
|vatAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of value-added tax on the line. The `totalAmount` field includes VAT, so the `vatAmount` can be<br>calculated with the formula `totalAmount × (vatRate / (100 + vatRate))`.<br><br>Any deviations from this will result in an error.<br><br>For example, for a `totalAmount` of SEK 100.00 with a 25.00% VAT rate, we expect a VAT amount of<br>`SEK 100.00 × (25 / 125) = SEK 20.00`.|
|sku|string|false|none|The SKU, EAN, ISBN or UPC of the product sold.|
|categories|[[line-categories](#schemaline-categories)]|false|none|An array with the voucher categories, in case of a line eligible for a voucher. See the<br>[Integrating Vouchers](https://docs.mollie.com/docs/integrating-vouchers/) guide for more information.|
|imageUrl|string|false|none|A link pointing to an image of the product sold.|
|productUrl|string|false|none|A link pointing to the product page in your web shop of the product sold.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|physical|
|type|digital|
|type|shipping_fee|
|type|discount|
|type|store_credit|
|type|gift_card|
|type|surcharge|
|type|tip|
|categories|eco|
|categories|gift|
|categories|meal|
|categories|sport_culture|
|categories|additional|
|categories|consume|

```json
{
  "title": "Mr.",

  "organizationName": "Mollie B.V.",
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the person, for example *Mr.* or *Mrs.*.|
|givenName|string|false|none|The given name (first name) of the person should be at least two characters and cannot contain only<br>numbers.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|
|familyName|string|false|none|The given family name (surname) of the person should be at least two characters and cannot contain only<br>numbers.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|
|organizationName|string|false|none|The name of the organization, in case the addressee is an organization.|
|streetAndNumber|string|false|none|A street and street number.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|
|streetAdditional|string|false|none|Any additional addressing details, for example an apartment number.|
|postalCode|string|false|none|A postal code. This field may be required if the provided country has a postal code system.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|
|email|string|false|none|A valid e-mail address.<br><br>If you provide the email address for a `banktransfer` payment, we will automatically send the instructions<br>email upon payment creation. The language of the email will follow the locale parameter of the payment.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.<br><br>If the domain contains non-ASCII characters, encode it as Punycode per [RFC 3492](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3492).|
|phone|string|false|none|If provided, it must be in the [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. For example: +31208202070.|
|city|string|false|none|A city name.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|
|region|string|false|none|The top-level administrative subdivision of the country. For example: Noord-Holland.|
|country|string|false|none|A country code in [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) format.<br><br>Required for payment methods `alma`, `billie`, `in3`, `klarna` and `riverty`.|

This object offers details about the status of a payment. Currently it is only available for point-of-sale
payments.

You can find more information about the possible values of this object on
[this page](status-reasons).**

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|object|true|none|none|
|message|string|true|none|A description of the status reason, localized according to the payment `locale`.|

An object containing payment details collected during the payment process. For example, details may include the
customer's card or bank details and a payment reference. For the full list of details, please refer to the
[method-specific parameters](extra-payment-parameters) guide.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|consumerName|string \| null|false|none|The customer's name, if made available by the payment method. For card payments, refer to `details.cardHolder`.|
|consumerAccount|string \| null|false|none|The customer's account reference.<br><br>For banking-based payment methods — such as iDEAL — this is normally either an IBAN or a domestic bank<br>account number.<br><br>For PayPal, the account reference is an email address.<br><br>For card and Bancontact payments, refer to `details.cardNumber`.|
|consumerBic|string \| null|false|none|The BIC of the customer's bank account, if applicable.|
|shippingAddress|object \| null|false|none|For wallet payment methods — such as Apple Pay and PayPal — the shipping address is often already known by<br>the wallet provider. In these cases the shipping address may be available as a payment detail.|
|cardNumber|string \| null|false|none|The customer's masked card number.|
|bankName|string|false|none|The name of the bank that the customer will need to make the bank transfer payment towards.|
|bankAccount|string|false|none|The bank account number the customer will need to make the bank transfer payment towards.|
|bankBic|string|false|none|The BIC of the bank the customer will need to make the bank transfer payment towards.|
|transferReference|string \| null|false|none|The Mollie-generated reference the customer needs to use when transfering the amount. Do not apply any<br>formatting here; show it to the customer as-is.|
|bizumReference|string \| null|false|none|Bizum payment reference of the transaction.|
|cardFingerprint|string \| null|false|none|A unique fingerprint for this specific card. Can be used to identify returning customers.|
|cardHolder|string \| null|false|none|The customer's name as shown on their card.|
|cardAudience|[payment-details-card-audition-response](#schemapayment-details-card-audition-response)|false|none|The card's target audience, if known.|
|cardLabel|[payment-details-card-label-response](#schemapayment-details-card-label-response)|false|none|The card's label, if known.|
|cardCountryCode|string \| null|false|none|The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the country the card was issued in.|
|cardExpiryDate|string \| null|false|none|The expiry date (`MM/YY`) of the card as displayed on the card.|
|cardFunding|[payment-details-card-funding-response](#schemapayment-details-card-funding-response)|false|none|The card type.|
|cardSecurity|[payment-details-card-security-response](#schemapayment-details-card-security-response)|false|none|The level of security applied during card processing.<br><br>Possible values: `normal` `3dsecure`|
|feeRegion|[payment-details-fee-region-response](#schemapayment-details-fee-region-response)|false|none|The applicable card fee region.|
|cardMaskedNumber|string \| null|false|none|The first6 and last4 digits of the card number.|
|card3dsEci|string \| null|false|none|The outcome of authentication attempted on transactions enforced by 3DS (ie valid only for `oneoff` and `first`).|
|cardBin|string \| null|false|none|The first6 digit of the card bank identification number.|
|cardIssuer|string \| null|false|none|The issuer of the Card.|
|failureReason|[payment-details-failure-reason-response](#schemapayment-details-failure-reason-response)|false|none|A failure code to help understand why the payment failed.|
|failureMessage|string \| null|false|none|A human-friendly failure message that can be shown to the customer. The message is translated in accordance<br>with the payment's locale setting.|
|wallet|[payment-details-wallet-response](#schemapayment-details-wallet-response)|false|none|The wallet used when creating the payment.|
|multibancoReference|string \| null|false|none|Multibanco payment reference of the transaction.|
|multibancoEntity|string \| null|false|none|Multibanco entity reference of the transaction.|
|paypalReference|string \| null|false|none|PayPal's reference for the payment.|
|paypalPayerId|string \| null|false|none|ID of the customer's PayPal account.|
|sellerProtection|[payment-details-seller-protection-response](#schemapayment-details-seller-protection-response)|false|none|Indicates to what extent the payment is eligible for PayPal's Seller Protection. Only available for PayPal<br>payments, if the information is made available by PayPal.<br><br>Classic values: `Eligible` `Ineligible` `Partially Eligible - INR Only`<br>`Partially Eligible - Unauth Only` `PartiallyEligible` `None` `Active`<br>`Fraud Control - Unauth Premium Eligible`<br><br>Current values: `ELIGIBLE` `PARTIALLY_ELIGIBLE` `NOT_ELIGIBLE`<br><br>_Note:_ Classic values are legacy and may still appear in older payments.|
|paypalFee|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|false|none|An amount object containing the fee PayPal will charge for this transaction. The field may be omitted if<br>PayPal will not charge a fee for this transaction.|
|customerReference|string|false|none|The paysafecard customer reference either provided via the API or otherwise auto-generated by Mollie.|
|terminalId|string|false|none|The ID of the terminal device where the payment took place on.|
|maskedNumber|string \| null|false|none|The first 6 digits & last 4 digits of the customer's masked card number.|
|creditorIdentifier|string \| null|false|none|The creditor identifier indicates who is authorized to execute the payment. In this case, it is a reference<br>to Mollie.|
|dueDate|string \| null(date)|false|none|Estimated date the payment is debited from the customer's bank account, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.|
|signatureDate|string \| null(date)|false|none|Date the payment has been signed by the customer, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Only available if the payment has<br>been signed.|
|bankReasonCode|string \| null|false|none|The official reason why this payment has failed. A detailed description of each reason is available on the<br>website of the European Payments Council.|
|bankReason|string \| null|false|none|A human-friendly description of the failure reason.|
|endToEndIdentifier|string \| null|false|none|The end-to-end identifier you provided in the batch file.|
|mandateReference|string \| null|false|none|The mandate reference you provided in the batch file.|
|batchReference|string \| null|false|none|The batch reference you provided in the batch file.|
|fileReference|string \| null|false|none|The file reference you provided in the batch file.|
|qrCode|object|false|none|**Optional include.** If a QR code was requested during payment creation for a QR-compatible payment method,<br>the QR code details will be available in this object.<br><br>The QR code can be scanned by the customer to complete the payment on their mobile device. For example,<br>Bancontact QR payments can be completed by the customer using the Bancontact app.<br><br>* `height` _integer_<br>* `width` _integer_<br>* `src` _string_|
|voucherNumber|string|false|none|For payments with gift cards: the masked gift card number of the first gift card applied to the payment.|
|giftcards|[object]|false|none|An array of detail objects for each gift card that was used on this payment, if any.|
|issuer|string|false|none|For payments with vouchers: the brand name of the first voucher applied.|
|vouchers|[object]|false|none|An array of detail objects for each voucher that was used on this payment, if any.|
|remainderAmount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|An amount object for the amount that remained after all gift cards or vouchers were applied.|
|remainderMethod|string|false|none|The payment method used to pay the remainder amount, after all gift cards or vouchers were applied.|
|remainderDetails|object|false|none|**Optional include.** The full payment method details of the remainder payment.|

<h2 id="tocS_testmode-create">testmode-create</h2>

<a id="schema_testmode-create"></a>
<a id="tocStestmode-create"></a>

```json
false
```

Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.

Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must
not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting
`testmode` to `true`.

The API will not reject strings longer than the maximum length but it will truncate them to fit.|

|cancelUrl|string \| null|false|none|The URL your customer will be redirected to when the customer explicitly cancels the payment. |Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|true|read-only|Indicates the response contains a payment object. Will always contain the string `payment` for this endpoint.|
|id|object|true|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this payment. Mollie assigns this identifier at payment creation time. Mollie<br>will always refer to the payment by this ID. Example: `tr_5B8cwPMGnU6qLbRvo7qEZo`.|
|mode|[mode](#schemamode)|true|read-only|Whether this entity was created in live mode or in test mode.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the payment will be shown to your customer on their card or bank statement when possible.<br>We truncate the description automatically according to the limits of the used payment method. The description is<br>also visible in any exports you generate.<br><br>We recommend you use a unique identifier so that you can always link the payment to the order in your back office.<br>This is particularly useful for bookkeeping.<br><br>The maximum length of the description field differs per payment method, with the absolute maximum being 255<br>characters. The API will not reject strings longer than the maximum length but it will truncate them to fit.|
|amount|[amount](#schemaamount)|true|none|The amount that you want to charge, e.g. `{currency:"EUR", value:"1000.00"}` if you would want to charge €1000.00.<br><br>You can find the minimum and maximum amounts per payment method in our help center. Additionally, they can be<br>retrieved using the Get method endpoint.<br><br>If a tip was added for a Point-of-Sale payment, the amount will be updated to reflect the initial amount plus the<br>tip amount.|
|amountRefunded|object|false|read-only|none|
|amountRemaining|object|false|read-only|none|
|amountCaptured|object|false|read-only|none|
|amountChargedBack|object|false|read-only|none|
|redirectUrl|string \| null|false|none|The URL your customer will be redirected to after the payment process.<br><br>It could make sense for the redirectUrl to contain a unique identifier – like your order ID – so you can show the<br>right page referencing the order when your customer returns.<br><br>The parameter is normally required, but can be omitted for recurring payments (`sequenceType: recurring`) and for<br>Apple Pay payments with an `applePayPaymentToken`.|
|cancelUrl|string \| null|false|none|The URL your customer will be redirected to when the customer explicitly cancels the payment. If this URL is not<br>provided, the customer will be redirected to the `redirectUrl` instead — see above.<br><br>Mollie will always give you status updates via webhooks, including for the canceled status. This parameter is<br>therefore entirely optional, but can be useful when implementing a dedicated customer-facing flow to handle<br>payment cancellations.|
|webhookUrl|string \| null|false|none|The webhook URL where we will send payment status updates to.<br><br>The webhookUrl is optional, but without a webhook you will miss out on important status changes to your payment.<br><br>The webhookUrl must be reachable from Mollie's point of view, so you cannot use `localhost`. If you want to use<br>webhook during development on `localhost`, you must use a tool like ngrok to have the webhooks delivered to your<br>local machine.|
|lines|[object]|false|none|Optionally provide the order lines for the payment. Each line contains details such as a description of the item<br>ordered and its price.<br><br>All lines must have the same currency as the payment.<br><br>Required for payment methods `billie`, `billink`, `in3`, `klarna`, `riverty` and `voucher`.|
|billingAddress|object|false|none|The customer's billing address details. We advise to provide these details to improve fraud protection and<br>conversion.<br><br>Should include `email` or a valid postal address consisting of `streetAndNumber`, `postalCode`, `city` and<br>`country`.<br><br>Required for payment method `alma`, `in3`, `klarna`, `billie`, `billink` and `riverty`.|
|shippingAddress|[payment-address](#schemapayment-address)|false|none|The customer's shipping address details. We advise to provide these details to improve fraud protection and<br>conversion.<br><br>Should include `email` or a valid postal address consisting of `streetAndNumber`, `postalCode`, `city` and<br>`country`.|
|locale|[locale-response](#schemalocale-response)|false|none|Allows you to preset the language to be used in the hosted payment pages shown to the customer. Setting a locale<br>is highly recommended and will greatly improve your conversion rate. When this parameter is omitted the browser<br>language will be used instead if supported by the payment method. You can provide any `xx_XX` format ISO 15897<br>locale, but our hosted payment pages currently only support the specified languages.<br><br>For bank transfer payments specifically, the locale will determine the target bank account the customer has to<br>transfer the money to. We have dedicated bank accounts for Belgium, Germany, and The Netherlands. Having the<br>customer use a local bank account greatly increases the conversion and speed of payment.|
|countryCode|string \| null|false|read-only|This optional field contains your customer's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, detected by us during checkout. This<br>field is omitted if the country code was not detected.|
|method|object|false|none|none|
|issuer|string \| null|false|write-only|**Only relevant for iDEAL, KBC/CBC, gift card, and voucher payments.**<br><br>**⚠️ With the introduction of iDEAL 2 in 2025, this field will be ignored for iDEAL payments. For more information<br>on the migration, refer to our [help center](https://help.mollie.com/hc/articles/19100313768338-iDEAL-2-0).**<br><br>Some payment methods are a network of connected banks or card issuers. In these cases, after selecting the payment<br>method, the customer may still need to select the appropriate issuer before the payment can proceed.<br><br>We provide hosted issuer selection screens, but these screens can be skipped by providing the `issuer` via the API<br>up front.<br><br>The full list of issuers for a specific method can be retrieved via the Methods API by using the optional<br>`issuers` include.<br><br>A valid issuer for iDEAL is for example `ideal_INGBNL2A` (for ING Bank).|
|restrictPaymentMethodsToCountry|string \| null|false|none|For digital goods in most jurisdictions, you must apply the VAT rate from your customer's country. Choose the VAT<br>rates you have used for the order to ensure your customer's country matches the VAT country.<br><br>Use this parameter to restrict the payment methods available to your customer to those from a single country.<br><br>If available, the credit card method will still be offered, but only cards from the allowed country are accepted.<br><br>The field expects a country code in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format, for example `NL`.|
|metadata|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|none|Provide any data you like, for example a string or a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity. Whenever<br>you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately 1kB.|
|captureMode|[capture-mode-response](#schemacapture-mode-response)|false|none|Indicate if the funds should be captured immediately or if you want to [place a hold](https://docs.mollie.com/docs/place-a-hold-for-a-payment#/) <br>and capture at a later time.<br><br>This field needs to be set to `manual` for method `riverty`.|
|captureDelay|string \| null|false|none|**Only relevant if you wish to manage authorization and capturing separately.**<br><br>Some payment methods allow placing a hold on the card or bank account. This hold or 'authorization' can then at a<br>later point either be 'captured' or canceled.<br><br>By default, we charge the customer's card or bank account immediately when they complete the payment. If you set a<br>capture delay however, we will delay the automatic capturing of the payment for the specified amount of time. For<br>example `8 hours` or `2 days`.<br><br>To schedule an automatic capture, the `captureMode` must be set to `automatic`.<br><br>The maximum delay is 7 days (168 hours).<br><br>Possible values: `... hours` `... days`|
|captureBefore|string \| null|false|read-only|Indicates the date before which the payment needs to be captured, in ISO 8601 format. From this date onwards we<br>can no longer guarantee a successful capture. The parameter is omitted if the payment is not authorized (yet).|
|applicationFee|object \| null|false|none|With Mollie Connect you can charge fees on payments that your app is processing on behalf of other Mollie<br>merchants.<br><br>If you use OAuth to create payments on a connected merchant's account, you can charge a fee using this<br>`applicationFee` parameter. If the payment succeeds, the fee will be deducted from the merchant's balance and sent<br>to your own account balance.<br><br>If instead you want to split a payment on your own account between yourself and a connected merchant, refer to the<br>`routing` parameter.|
|routing|[[entity-payment-route-response](#schemaentity-payment-route-response)]|false|none|*This functionality is not enabled by default. Reach out to our partner management team if you wish to use it.*<br><br>With Mollie Connect you can charge fees on payments that your app is processing on behalf of other Mollie<br>merchants.<br><br>If you create payments on your own account that you want to split between yourself and one or more connected<br>merchants, you can use this `routing` parameter to route the payment accordingly.<br><br>The `routing` parameter should contain an array of objects, with each object describing the destination for a<br>specific portion of the payment.<br><br>It is not necessary to indicate in the array which portion goes to yourself. After all portions of the total<br>payment amount have been routed, the amount left will be routed to the current organization automatically.<br><br>If instead you use OAuth to create payments on a connected merchant's account, refer to the `applicationFee`<br>parameter.|
|sequenceType|[sequence-type-response](#schemasequence-type-response)|true|none|**Only relevant for recurring payments.**<br><br>Indicate which part of a recurring sequence this payment is for.<br><br>Recurring payments can only take place if a mandate is available. A common way to establish such a mandate is<br>through a `first` payment. With a `first` payment, the customer agrees to automatic recurring charges taking place<br>on their account in the future.<br><br>If set to `recurring`, the customer's card is charged automatically.<br><br>Defaults to `oneoff`, which is a regular non-recurring payment.<br><br>For PayPal payments, recurring is only possible if your connected PayPal account allows it. You can call our<br>[Methods API](list-methods) with parameter `sequenceType: first` to discover which payment methods on your account<br>are set up correctly for recurring payments.|
|subscriptionId|string \| null|false|read-only|If the payment was automatically created via a subscription, the ID of the [subscription](get-subscription) will<br>be added to the response.|
|mandateId|string \| null|false|none|**Only relevant for recurring payments and stored cards.**<br><br>When creating recurring or stored cards payments, the ID of a specific [mandate](get-mandate) can be supplied to indicate which of<br>the customer's accounts should be debited.|
|customerId|[customerToken](#schemacustomertoken)|false|none|The ID of the [customer](get-customer) the payment is being created for. This is used primarily for recurring<br>payments, but can also be used on regular payments to enable single-click payments.<br><br>If `sequenceType` is set to `recurring`, this field is required.|
|profileId|[profileToken](#schemaprofiletoken)|true|none|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) this entity belongs to.<br><br>When using an API Key, the `profileId` must not be sent since it is linked to the key. However, for OAuth and<br>Organization tokens, the `profileId` is required.<br><br>For more information, see [Authentication](authentication).|
|settlementId|string \| null|false|read-only|The identifier referring to the [settlement](get-settlement) this payment was settled with.|
|orderId|string \| null|false|read-only|If the payment was created for an [order](get-order), the ID of that order will be part of the response.|
|status|object|true|read-only|none|
|statusReason|[status-reason](#schemastatus-reason)|false|read-only|This object offers details about the status of a payment. Currently it is only available for point-of-sale<br>payments.<br><br>You can find more information about the possible values of this object on<br>[this page](status-reasons).**|
|isCancelable|boolean \| null|false|read-only|Whether the payment can be canceled. This parameter is omitted if the payment reaches a final state.|
|details|[payment-details](#schemapayment-details)|false|read-only|An object containing payment details collected during the payment process. For example, details may include the<br>customer's card or bank details and a payment reference. For the full list of details, please refer to the<br>[method-specific parameters](extra-payment-parameters) guide.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|true|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|authorizedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment became authorized, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment is<br>not authorized (yet).|
|paidAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment became paid, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment is not<br>completed (yet).|
|canceledAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment was canceled, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment is not<br>canceled (yet).|
|expiresAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment will expire, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment can no<br>longer expire.|
|expiredAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment was expired, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment did not<br>expire (yet).|
|failedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment failed, in ISO 8601 format. This parameter is omitted if the payment did not fail<br>(yet).|
|dueDate|string \| null|false|write-only|The date by which the payment should be completed in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Sending `null` has the same effect<br>as omitting the field.|
|storeCredentials|boolean|false|write-only|Whether the card details should be stored for the customer after a successful payment. This will create a mandate for the customer, <br>allowing for future customer present saved-card CIT payments. Requires customerId, cardToken, and the creditcard method to be specified. |
|testmode|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|write-only|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|
|_links|object|true|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|
|method|[method-response](#schemamethod-response)|false|none|The payment method used for this transaction. If a specific method was selected during payment initialization,<br>this field reflects that choice.|

<h2 id="tocS_settlement-mode">settlement-mode</h2>


Whether this entity was created in live mode or in test mode. Settlements are always in live mode.

```json
"dutch"
```

Mollie applies Dutch VAT for merchants based in The Netherlands, British VAT for merchants based in The United
Kingdom, and shifted VAT for merchants in the European Union.

The field is not present for merchants residing in other countries.

<h2 id="tocS_profile-status">profile-status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprofile-status"></a>
<a id="schema_profile-status"></a>
<a id="tocSprofile-status"></a>
<a id="tocsprofile-status"></a>

```json
"unverified"
```

The profile status determines whether the profile is able to receive live payments.

* `unverified`: The profile has not been verified yet and can only be used to create test payments.
* `verified`: The profile has been verified and can be used to create live payments and test payments.
* `blocked`: The profile is blocked and can no longer be used or changed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The name of this requirement, referring to the task to be fulfilled by the organization<br>to enable or re-enable the capability. The name is unique among other requirements<br>of the same capability. Examples include `needs-data` and `process-first-payment`.|
|status|[capability-requirement-status](#schemacapability-requirement-status)|true|none|The status of the requirement depends on its due date.<br>If no due date is given, the status will be `requested`.|
|dueDate|string \| null|true|none|Due date until the requirement must be fulfilled, if any. The date is shown in ISO-8601 format.|
|_links|object|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|currently-due|
|status|past-due|
|status|requested|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|false|read-only|Indicates the response contains a payment link object. Will always contain the string `payment-link` for this<br>endpoint.|
|id|object|false|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this payment link. Example: `pl_4Y0eZitmBnQ6IDoMqZQKh`.|
|mode|[mode](#schemamode)|false|read-only|Whether this entity was created in live mode or in test mode.|
|description|string|false|none|A short description of the payment link. The description is visible in the Dashboard and will be shown on the<br>customer's bank or card statement when possible.|
|amount|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|false|none|The amount of the payment link. If no amount is provided initially, the customer will be prompted to enter an<br>amount.|
|minimumAmount|[amount-nullable](#schemaamount-nullable)|false|none|The minimum amount of the payment link. This property is only allowed when there is no amount provided. The<br>customer will be prompted to enter a value greater than or equal to the minimum amount.|
|archived|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the payment link is archived. Customers will not be able to complete payments on archived payment links.|
|redirectUrl|string \| null|false|none|The URL your customer will be redirected to after completing the payment process. If no redirect URL is provided,<br>the customer will be shown a generic message after completing the payment.|
|webhookUrl|string \| null|false|none|The webhook URL where we will send payment status updates to.<br><br>The webhookUrl is optional, but without a webhook you will miss out on important status changes to any payments<br>resulting from the payment link.<br><br>The webhookUrl must be reachable from Mollie's point of view, so you cannot use `localhost`. If you want to use<br>webhook during development on `localhost`, you must use a tool like ngrok to have the webhooks delivered to your<br>local machine.|
|lines|[[payment-line-item-response](#schemapayment-line-item-response)]|false|none|Optionally provide the order lines for the payment. Each line contains details such as a description of the item<br>ordered and its price.<br><br>All lines must have the same currency as the payment.<br><br>Required for payment methods `billie`, `in3`, `klarna`, `riverty` and `voucher`.|
|billingAddress|[payment-address](#schemapayment-address)|false|none|The customer's billing address details. We advise to provide these details to improve fraud protection and<br>conversion.<br><br>Should include `email` or a valid postal address consisting of `streetAndNumber`, `postalCode`, `city` and<br>`country`.<br><br>Required for payment method `in3`, `klarna`, `billie` and `riverty`.|
|shippingAddress|[payment-address](#schemapayment-address)|false|none|The customer's shipping address details. We advise to provide these details to improve fraud protection and<br>conversion.<br><br>Should include `email` or a valid postal address consisting of `streetAndNumber`, `postalCode`, `city` and<br>`country`.|
|profileId|string \| null|false|none|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) this entity belongs to.<br><br>Most API credentials are linked to a single profile. In these cases the `profileId` must not be sent in the creation<br>request. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens however, the `profileId` parameter is<br>required.|
|reusable|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates whether the payment link is reusable. If this field is set to `true`, customers can make multiple<br>payments using the same link.<br><br>If no value is specified, the field defaults to `false`, allowing only a single payment per link.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|paidAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the payment link became paid, in ISO 8601 format.|
|expiresAt|string \| null|false|none|The date and time the payment link is set to expire, in ISO 8601 format. If no expiry date was provided up front,<br>the payment link will not expire automatically.|
|allowedMethods|[payment-link-methods-response](#schemapayment-link-methods-response)|false|none|An array of payment methods that are allowed to be used for this payment link. When this parameter is<br>not provided or is an empty array, all enabled payment methods will be available.|
|applicationFee|object|false|none|With Mollie Connect you can charge fees on payment links that your app is processing on behalf of other Mollie<br>merchants.<br><br>If you use OAuth to create payment links on a connected merchant's account, you can charge a fee using this<br>`applicationFee` parameter. If a payment on the payment link succeeds, the fee will be deducted from the merchant's balance and sent<br>to your own account balance.|
|sequenceType|[payment-link-sequence-type-response](#schemapayment-link-sequence-type-response)|false|none|If set to `first`, a payment mandate is established right after a payment is made by the customer.<br><br>Defaults to `oneoff`, which is a regular payment link and will not establish a mandate after payment.<br><br>The mandate ID can be retrieved by making a call to the<br>[Payment Link Payments Endpoint](get-payment-link-payments).|
|customerId|string \| null|false|none|**Only relevant when `sequenceType` is set to `first`**<br><br>The ID of the [customer](get-customer) the payment link is being created for. If a value is not provided,<br>the customer will be required to input relevant information which will be used to establish a mandate after<br>the payment is made.|
|testmode|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|write-only|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|
|_links|object|false|read-only|An object with several relevant URLs. Every URL object will contain an `href` and a `type` field.|

|profileId|string \| null|false|none|The identifier referring to the [profile](get-profile) this entity belongs to.<br><br>Most API credentials are linked to a single profile. In these cases the `profileId` must not be sent in the creation<br>request. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens however, the `profileId` parameter is<br>required.|
|status|string|false|none|none|

|vatScheme|[sales-invoice-vat-scheme](#schemasales-invoice-vat-scheme)|false|none|The VAT scheme to create the invoice for. You must be enrolled with One Stop Shop enabled to use it.|
|vatMode|[sales-invoice-vat-mode](#schemasales-invoice-vat-mode)|false|none|The VAT mode to use for VAT calculation. `exclusive` mode means we will apply the relevant VAT on top of the<br>price. `inclusive` means the prices you are providing to us already contain the VAT you want to apply.|
|memo|string \| null|false|none|A free-form memo you can set on the invoice, and will be shown on the invoice PDF.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Provide any data you like as a JSON object. We will save the data alongside the entity. Whenever<br>you fetch the entity with our API, we will also include the metadata. You can use up to approximately 1kB.|
|paymentTerm|[sales-invoice-payment-term](#schemasales-invoice-payment-term)|false|none|The payment term to be set on the invoice.|
|paymentDetails|object|false|none|Used when setting an invoice to status of `paid`, and will store a payment that fully pays the invoice with the<br>provided details. Required for `paid` status.|
|emailDetails|[sales-invoice-email-details](#schemasales-invoice-email-details)|false|none|Used when setting an invoice to status of either `issued` or `paid`. Will be used to issue the invoice to the<br>recipient with the provided `subject` and `body`. Required for `issued` status.|
|customerId|string|false|none|The identifier referring to the [customer](get-customer) you want to attempt an automated payment for. If<br>provided, `mandateId` becomes required as well. Only allowed for invoices with status `paid`.|
|mandateId|string|false|none|The identifier referring to the [mandate](get-mandate) you want to use for the automated payment. If provided,<br>`customerId` becomes required as well. Only allowed for invoices with status `paid`.|
|recipientIdentifier|string|false|none|An identifier tied to the recipient data. This should be a unique value based on data your system contains,<br>so that both you and us know who we're referring to. It is a value you provide to us so that recipient management<br>is not required to send a first invoice to a recipient.|
|recipient|[sales-invoice-recipient](#schemasales-invoice-recipient)|false|none|none|
|lines|[[sales-invoice-line-item](#schemasales-invoice-line-item)]|false|none|Provide the line items for the invoice. Each line contains details such as a description of the item<br>ordered and its price.<br><br>All lines must have the same currency as the invoice.|
|discount|[sales-invoice-discount](#schemasales-invoice-discount)|false|none|The discount to be applied to the entire invoice, applied on top of any line item discounts.|
|isEInvoice|boolean|false|none|This indicates whether the invoice is an e-invoice. The default value is `false` and can't be changed<br>after the invoice has been issued. When `emailDetails` is provided, an additional email is sent to the<br>recipient.<br><br>E-invoicing is only available for merchants based in Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands, and only when<br>the recipient is also located in one of these countries.<br><br>When set to true, the invoice will be delivered via the Peppol network. In this case, the organizationNumber<br>or vatNumber provided must match the identifier the recipient is actually registered with on Peppol,<br>otherwise delivery will fail. Note: for recipients in Germany, the vatNumber is the required identifier<br>for Peppol registration.|
|amountDue|object|false|read-only|none|
|subtotalAmount|object|false|read-only|none|
|totalAmount|object|false|read-only|none|
|totalVatAmount|object|false|read-only|none|
|discountedSubtotalAmount|object|false|read-only|none|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|issuedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|If issued, the date when the sales invoice was issued, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format.|
|paidAt|string \| null|false|read-only|If paid, the date when the sales invoice was paid, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format.|
|dueAt|string \| null|false|read-only|If issued, the date when the sales invoice payment is due, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format.|

A human-readable reason explaining the current status of the transfer. Only populated when the transfer has
reached a terminal status of `failed`, `rejected`, or `blocked`.

This field is `null` for transfers that have not reached one of these statuses.

<a id="schemadraft-transfer-status-reason-code"></a>
<a id="schema_draft-transfer-status-reason-code"></a>
<a id="tocSdraft-transfer-status-reason-code"></a>

```json
"deleted-by-creator"
```

A machine-readable code that indicates the reason for the draft transfer's current status.

<h2 id="tocS_draft-transfer-status-reason">draft-transfer-status-reason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadraft-transfer-status-reason"></a>
<a id="schema_draft-transfer-status-reason"></a>
<a id="tocSdraft-transfer-status-reason"></a>
<a id="tocsdraft-transfer-status-reason"></a>

```json
{
  "code": "deleted-by-creator",
  "message": "The draft transfer has been deleted by the user who created it"
}
```

The reason for the draft transfer's current status. `null` unless `status` is `declined`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|[draft-transfer-status-reason-code-response](#schemadraft-transfer-status-reason-code-response)|true|none|A machine-readable code that indicates the reason for the draft transfer's current status.|
|message|string|true|none|A human-readable explanation of the status reason. For `declined-by-initiator`, this includes the<br>initiator's free-text reason when they provided one.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|deleted-by-creator|
|code|declined-by-initiator|
|code|account-closed|

```json
{
  "resource": "business-account-draft-transfer",
  "id": {},
  "mode": "live",
  "debtorIban": "NL55MLLE0123456789",
  "debtor": {
    "fullName": "Jan Jansen",
    "account": {
      "iban": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
    }
  },
  "creditor": {
    "fullName": "Jan Jansen",
    "account": {
      "iban": "NL02ABNA0123456789"
    }
  },
  "amount": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "value": "10.00"
  },
  "description": "Invoice 12345",
  "scheduledExecutionDate": "2025-03-01",
  "status": {},
  "statusReason": {
    "code": "deleted-by-creator",
    "message": "The draft transfer has been deleted by the user who created it"
  },
  "createdAt": "2024-03-20T09:13:37+00:00",
  "approvedAt": "2025-01-01T12:05:00+00:00",
  "declinedAt": "2025-01-01T12:05:00+00:00",
  "deletedAt": "2025-01-01T12:05:00+00:00",
  "testmode": false,
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "https://api.mollie.com/v2/business-accounts/draft-transfers/badrt_87GByBuj4UCcUTEbs6aGJ",
      "type": "application/hal+json"
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource|string|false|read-only|Indicates the response contains a draft transfer object. Will always contain the string<br>`business-account-draft-transfer` for this endpoint.|
|id|object|false|read-only|The identifier uniquely referring to this draft transfer. Mollie assigns this identifier at draft transfer<br>creation time.|
|mode|[mode](#schemamode)|false|read-only|Whether this entity was created in live mode or in test mode.|
|debtorIban|string|false|write-only|The IBAN of the debtor's (sender) Mollie Business Account.|
|debtor|object|false|read-only|The debtor (sender) of the draft transfer, resolved from `debtorIban` at creation time.|
|creditor|[draft-transfer-party](#schemadraft-transfer-party)|false|none|The creditor (recipient) of the draft transfer, including their name and account details.|
|amount|[amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the draft transfer, e.g. `{"currency":"EUR", "value":"100.00"}` if you would want to transfer<br>€100.00.<br><br>Only `EUR` is supported.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A short description of the draft transfer. Once approved, this will appear on the bank statement of both<br>the debtor and creditor.|
|scheduledExecutionDate|string \| null(date)|false|none|The date on which the resulting transfer will be executed, once approved. Defaults to same-day if omitted,<br>in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date format.|
|status|object|false|read-only|none|
|statusReason|[draft-transfer-status-reason](#schemadraft-transfer-status-reason)|false|read-only|The reason for the draft transfer's current status. `null` unless `status` is `declined`.|
|createdAt|[created-at](#schemacreated-at)|false|read-only|The entity's date and time of creation, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format.|
|approvedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the draft transfer was approved, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)<br>format. `null` unless `status` is `approved`.|
|declinedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the draft transfer was declined by the initiator, in [ISO<br>8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. `null` unless `statusReason.code` is<br>`declined-by-initiator`.|
|deletedAt|string \| null|false|read-only|The date and time the draft transfer was deleted via the [Cancel draft transfer](cancel-draft-transfer)<br>endpoint, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. `null` unless `statusReason.code` is<br>`deleted-by-creator`.|
|testmode|[testmode-create](#schematestmode-create)|false|write-only|Whether to create the entity in test mode or live mode.<br><br>Most API credentials are specifically created for either live mode or test mode, in which case this parameter must<br>not be sent. For organization-level credentials such as OAuth access tokens, you can enable test mode by setting<br>`testmode` to `true`.|
|_links|object|false|read-only|Links to related resources.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|live|
|mode|test|
